2.4.m: Homage to holy Gaṇeśa.
Now begins the Kārttikamāsamāhātmya.
Having bowed to Nārāyaṇa, and to Nara, the best of men,
and also to the goddess Sarasvatī, one should then utter 'Success!' 1
The seers said:

2.4.s: sūta naḥ kathitaṃ puṇyaṃ māhātmyamāśvinasya ca ..
2.4.d: सूत नः कथितं पुण्यं माहात्म्यमाश्विनस्य च ..
2.4.m: O Sūta, you have told us the holy māhātmya of Āśvina;
we wish to hear further another thing: the grandeur of Kārtika. 2
In the Kali [age], for men of defiled minds and sinful deeds,
plunged in the ocean of transmigration, what is the effortless refuge? 3
Which duty of all duties is superior, accomplishing liberation
and bestowing liberation on men even in this world? Tell this, O lord! 4
Sūta said:
That which you have asked me, the sage Nārada,

2.4.s: nārado brahmaṇaḥ putro brahmāṇaṃ tu jagadgurum .. 5 ..
2.4.d: नारदो ब्रह्मणः पुत्रो ब्रह्माणं तु जगद्गुरुम् .. 5 ..
2.4.m: the son of Brahmā, asked Brahmā, the teacher of the world; 5
and likewise Satyabhāmā [asked] holy Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the universe.
[So too Satyabhāmā,] eager to hear, questioned [Śrī Kṛṣṇa] about the glory of Kārtika.
And what was spoken by the Vālakhilya seers in the assembly of seers,
in the exceedingly charming form of a dialogue between the venerable Sūrya and Aruṇa;
and the glory of Kārtika [told] on Mount Kailāsa by Śaṃkara,
described before the Six-Faced One [Skanda], accompanied by diverse narratives;

2.4.s: pṛthuṃ prati nāradena kathitaṃ ca mahātmyakam ..
2.4.d: पृथुं प्रति नारदेन कथितं च महात्म्यकम् ..
2.4.m: and the greatness told by Nārada to Pṛthu
concerning Kārtika, O leaders of brahmins, after having heard it from the mouth of Brahmā long ago:
Once, Nārada the yogin went to Satyaloka
and asked the Grandfather of all the worlds with utmost humility:
Śrī Nārada said:
Of the terrible firewood of sin, dry and wet in great abundance,
what fire burns it up, O Brahmā? You ought to tell that.
Nothing within the cosmic egg, among the three worlds,
is unknown to you, O Lord of the gods, certainly of three kinds.
Tell [me] the best month among months, the highest among gods,
and especially the sacred fords, O Grandfather.
Brahmā said:
Among months, Kārtika is best; among gods, Madhusūdana;

2.4.s: tīrthaṃ nārāyaṇākhyaṃ hi tritayaṃ durlabhaṃ kalau .. 14 ..
2.4.d: तीर्थं नारायणाख्यं हि त्रितयं दुर्लभं कलौ .. 14 ..
2.4.m: the sacred ford named Nārāyaṇa—indeed, this triad is rare to attain in the Kali age.
Nārada said:
O Lord, I am your servant, I am your devotee, O beloved of Hari!
Speak to me of the Vaiṣṇava dharmas; you are omniscient, O Grandfather.
First, O Lord, you ought to tell me the māhātmya of Kārtika,
the māhātmya of offering lamps, and the observances of those who undertake vows,
and the māhātmya of gopīcandana, and likewise of Tulasī, O Lord,

2.4.s: dhātryāścaiva ca māhātmyaṃ vidhiṃ snānādikasya ca ..
2.4.d: धात्र्याश्चैव च माहात्म्यं विधिं स्नानादिकस्य च ..
2.4.m: and the māhātmya of the Dhātrī tree, and the rite of ritual ablutions and the like;
when the commencement of the vow is to be made, and the rule for concluding the observance;
whatever Vaiṣṇava duty there is, you ought to tell all of that,
by which, through your grace, I may go to the painless state.
Sūta said:
Hearing these words of his son, Brahmā was filled with joy;
remembering Rādhā-Dāmodara, he spoke to his son:
Brahmā said:
Well asked by you, O son, for the sake of uplifting the world!

2.4.s: kathayāmi na saṃdehaḥ kārtikasya ca vaibhavam .. 2.4.1.20 ..
2.4.d: कथयामि न संदेहः कार्तिकस्य च वैभवम् .. 2.4.1.20 ..
2.4.m: Without a doubt, I shall speak of the glory of Kārtika.
On one side, all sacred fords and all sacrifices with their sacrificial fees;

2.4.s: kārtikasya tu māsasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm .. 21 ..
2.4.d: कार्तिकस्य तु मासस्य कलां नार्हंति षोडशीम् .. 21 ..
2.4.m: yet they do not equal a sixteenth part of the month of Kārtika.
On one side, residence at Puṣkara, Kurukṣetra, and the Himālayas;
on the other, O son, Kārtika is deemed to surpass all merit.
Gold equal [in size] to Mount Meru and all donations on one side;
on the other, O dear one, Kārtika, which is always dear to Keśava.
Whatever merit is performed dedicated to Viṣṇu in Kārtika,

2.4.s: tasya kṣayaṃ na paśyāmi mayoktaṃ tava nārada .. 24 ..
2.4.d: तस्य क्षयं न पश्यामि मयोक्तं तव नारद .. 24 ..
2.4.m: I see no end to it; this has been declared by me to you, O Nārada.
Having obtained the human state, difficult to attain, which is a stairway to heaven,
one should compose oneself in such a way that one does not fall again.

2.4.s: duṣprāpyaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ kārtikoktaṃ carenna yaḥ ..
2.4.d: दुष्प्राप्यं प्राप्य मानुष्यं कार्तिकोक्तं चरेन्न यः ..
2.4.m: He who, having attained the human state difficult to obtain, does not practice
the duty enjoined in Kārtika, O best among upholders of dharma, is a slayer of mother and father.

2.4.s: kārtikaḥ khalu vai māsaḥ sarvamāseṣu cottamaḥ ..
2.4.d: कार्तिकः खलु वै मासः सर्वमासेषु चोत्तमः ..
2.4.m: The month of Kārtika indeed is the best among all months,

2.4.s: puṇyānāṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ pāvanānāṃ ca pāvanam .. 27 ..
2.4.d: पुण्यानां परमं पुण्यं पावनानां च पावनम् .. 27 ..
2.4.m: the supreme merit among merits, the purifier of purifiers.
In this month the thirty-three gods are present, O sage;
here ritual ablutions, gifts, feedings, and vows [are performed].
A cow made of sesame seeds, gold, silver, land, clothing,
and gifts of cattle, they perform with wholehearted feeling, O Nārada.
Those gifts given, the gods accept according to rule.

2.4.s: yatkiṃca dattaṃ vipreṃdra tapaścaiva tathā kṛtam .. 2.4.1.30 ..
2.4.d: यत्किंच दत्तं विप्रेंद्र तपश्चैव तथा कृतम् .. 2.4.1.30 ..
2.4.m: Whatever is given, O leader of brahmins, and austerity likewise performed,
that has been declared imperishable in fruit by the mighty Viṣṇu.

2.4.s: pāpānāṃ mokṣaṇaṃ caiva kārtike māsi śasyate .. 31 ..
2.4.d: पापानां मोक्षणं चैव कार्तिके मासि शस्यते .. 31 ..
2.4.m: And the release from sins is praised in the month of Kārtika;
therefore, O leader of brahmins, [charity] is diligently given in the month of Kārtika.
Whatever is given in Kārtika dedicated to Viṣṇu by men,
that indeed obtains imperishable [reward], especially the gift of food.

2.4.s: yathā nadīnāṃ vipreṃdra śailānāṃ caiva nārada .. 33 ..
2.4.d: यथा नदीनां विप्रेंद्र शैलानां चैव नारद .. 33 ..
2.4.m: Just as with rivers, O leader of brahmins, and with mountains, O Nārada,
and with oceans, O brahmin-seer, no destruction is ever possible,
whatever gift is given in the month of Kārtika, O sage,

2.4.s: na tasyāsti kṣayo vipra pāpaṃ yāti sahasradhā ..
2.4.d: न तस्यास्ति क्षयो विप्र पापं याति सहस्रधा ..
2.4.m: has no diminution, O brahmin; sin departs in a thousand ways.

2.4.s: saṃprāptaṃ kārtikaṃ dṛṣṭvā parānnaṃ yastu varjayet ..35..
2.4.d: संप्राप्तं कार्तिकं दृष्ट्वा परान्नं यस्तु वर्जयेत् ..35..
2.4.m: Seeing Kārtika arrived, whoever avoids food given by others
effortlessly obtains the fruit of an Atikṛcchra penance day by day.

2.4.s: na kārtikasamo māso na kṛtena samaṃ yugam ..36..
2.4.d: न कार्तिकसमो मासो न कृतेन समं युगम् ..36..
2.4.m: There is no month equal to Kārtika; there is no yuga equal to Kṛta;

2.4.s: na vedasadṛśaṃ śāstraṃ na tīrthaṃ gaṃgayā samam ..
2.4.d: न वेदसदृशं शास्त्रं न तीर्थं गंगया समम् ..
2.4.m: there is no scripture like the Veda; there is no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā;

2.4.s: na cānnasadṛśaṃ dānaṃ na sukhaṃ bhāryayā samam .. 37 ..
2.4.d: न चान्नसदृशं दानं न सुखं भार्यया समम् .. 37 ..
2.4.m: there is no gift like [the gift of] food; there is no happiness like [that with] a wife.
Wealth acquired by lawful means is rare for those who give gifts;
and giving it at a sacred ford is rare for mortals by nature.
In Kārtika, O tiger among sages, worship of the Śāligrāma stone
and remembrance of Vāsudeva should be performed by one who fears sin.

2.4.s: etādṛśaṃ kārtikaṃ ca akṛtenaiva yo nayet ..
2.4.d: एतादृशं कार्तिकं च अकृतेनैव यो नयेत् ..
2.4.m: Whoever spends such a Kārtika having done nothing at all,
undoubtedly attains the destruction of merit previously acquired. // 2.4.1.40
Nārada said:
How should the supreme Kārtika observance be performed by one who is incapable?
Tell me that, O Grandfather, whereby he may obtain its fruit. // 41
Brahmā said:
When a mortal is incapable, he should then observe the vow in this manner:
giving wealth to another, he should have the Kārtika observance performed [by him]. // 42
He should accept merit from him preceded by the solemn resolve of giving.
If he is incapable even of giving wealth, O best of divine seers, // 43

2.4.s: tadā tena prakartavyaṃ pānaṃ tīrthajalasya ca ..
2.4.d: तदा तेन प्रकर्तव्यं पानं तीर्थजलस्य च ..
2.4.m: then the drinking of the water of a sacred ford should be performed by him.
The mortal who is incapable even of that should joyfully and regularly
remember Hari by name according to fixed rule; // 44
then the unbroken fruit arising from the Kārtika observance is [gained] by him. // 45
He should keep the night-vigil of Hari in a temple of Viṣṇu or of Śiva;
in the absence of an abode of Śiva or Viṣṇu, even in temples of all deities. // 46
Or if he is situated in an impenetrable forest or has fallen into distress,
he should perform it at the foot of an Aśvattha tree or in groves of tulasī. // 47
A human who sings compositions of Viṣṇu's names in the presence of Viṣṇu
obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows. // 48
And a man who plays musical instruments obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice;
a dancer obtains the fruit arising from bathing in all sacred fords. // 49
The man who gives wealth to these obtains all this merit;
or from hearing or from seeing, one may obtain a sixth part of the fruit. // 2.4.1.50
Even when fallen into distress, if a man cannot find water anywhere,
or if he is afflicted by illness, he should perform sprinkling [purification] with the name of Viṣṇu. // 51
One established in the vow who is incapable of performing the concluding rite
should feed brahmins afterwards for the sake of the complete fulfillment of the vow. // 52
Incapable of offering a lamp, he should kindle another's lamp,
or carefully protect it from the wind and other [disturbances]. // 53
In the absence of worship of Śrī Viṣṇu, worship of tulasī and the dhātrī tree [should be performed];
in the absence of all [these], the observer of the vow should perform [worship] of brahmins and cows;
in the absence even of that, the chanting of Viṣṇu's name in the mind. // 54
Nārada said:
O Brahmā, tell in detail the religious duties arising in Kārtika. // 55

2.4.m:
Thus ends the first chapter, named Description of the Praise of the Kārtika Observance, in the Praise of the Month of Kārtika in the second, Vaiṣṇava Section of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa in the compilation of eighty-one thousand [verses]. // 1
Brahmā said:
Now I shall declare the duties of the month of Kārtika, O Nārada.
Whoever, seeing that Kārtika has arrived, refrains from another's food,
attains liberation; of this there is no doubt.
Worship of the guru is considered supreme above all duties.
By serving the guru, one attains everything, O best of seers.
When the guru is pleased, all the gods along with Indra are pleased;
and when the guru is angry, all the gods along with Indra are angry.
When the month of Kārtika has arrived, though performing abundant rites,
if one does not perform service to the guru, one finds only hells.
Whatever one is commanded by the guru, one should carry out.
O brahmin, when ordered by the guru, one should not transgress his word.
If sorrow and the like befall, one should take refuge in the guru.

2.4.m:
and the gift of knowledge is equal to thousands of gifts of gold.
The gift of land is superior to the gift of knowledge by a crore times;
and the gift of a cow is superior to a thousand gifts of land;
and the gift of food is indeed superior to thousands of gifts of cows.
This [world] is declared to be founded on food; therefore it must be given in Kārtika.
Merely by avoiding another's food, one obtains the fruit of a Cāndrāyaṇa fast;
day by day a man obtains the fruit of an Atikṛcchra penance.
In Kārtika one should avoid meat, and fermented foods in particular;
by eating meat even once, one attains the womb of a rākṣasa.
When a restriction is observed in Kārtika regarding foods customarily indulged in,
one inevitably attains the form of Viṣṇu, the state that bestows liberation.
The fruit one obtains by giving land to brahmins during an eclipse of the sun or moon,
that fruit belongs to one who sleeps on the ground, my child.
Feeding a brahmin couple and honoring them with unguents,
blankets, jewels, and garments of various kinds,

give shoes and an umbrella in Kārtika, O you of good vows.
One who sleeps on the ground in Kārtika destroys sin accumulated over an age.
Whoever keeps a night vigil in the month of Kārtika at dawn,
before Dāmodara, O divine seer, obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.
A bath in a river, a discourse about Viṣṇu, and darśana of Vaiṣṇavas—
for one to whom these do not happen in Kārtika, it takes away ten years of merit.
The wise person who remembers Puṣkara in deed, mind, and speech
in Kārtika, O tiger among sages, finds it multiplied a hundred thousand and a crore times.
Prayāga in the month of Māgha, Puṣkara likewise in Kārtika,
and Avantī in the month of Mādhava destroy sin accumulated over an age.
Blessed are those men in the world, especially in the Kali age,
who constantly perform worship of Hari to please him.
By them their ancestors are delivered from hell; of this there is no doubt.
A ceremonial bath of Viṣṇu with milk and other substances performed for the sake of the ancestors:
having reached heaven for a crore of kalpas, they dwell along with the gods.

2.4.m:
Those by whom lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa is not worshipped in Kārtika,
in crores of births, O chief of brahmins, Kamalā does not dwell in their home.
Ah, robbed and ruined are those who have fallen into the cavern of the Kali [age],
by whom Hari was not worshipped with devotion using blue and white lotuses. (31)
Whoever worships the Lord of gods, the husband of Kamalā, with a single lotus,
destroys the sin of tens of millions of years.
By virtue of worship with a lotus, Śveta indeed attained liberation. (32)
Seven hundred and a thousand offenses
the Lord of gods forgives when bowed down to and worshipped with a single lotus. (33)
Whoever worships Hari in the month of Kārtika with a hundred thousand tulasī leaves,
obtains, O best of sages, the fruit of a pearl for every leaf. (34)
Whoever wears on the mouth, head, or body [leaves] taken down from Kṛṣṇa,
or cleanses their limbs with the tulasī remnants [offered to] Kṛṣṇa,
that person becomes freed from all diseases and sins. (35)
Conch water, devotion to Hari, the remnants of offerings, the water from [his] feet,
sandalwood paste, and the remainder of incense destroy [even] the murder of a brahmin. (36)

Devoted to morning ritual ablution in the month of Kārtika, O best of brahmins,
one should give food to brahmins according to one’s capacity. (37)
Of all gifts, the gift of food is pre-eminent:
the world is born through food, and through food alone does it grow. (38)
For the wise know that food is the supreme breath of life for all living beings.
One who gives food gives everything in the world and becomes a performer of all sacrifices. (39)
What need has he of bathing at a sacred ford? What need even of pilgrimages to gods and the like?
Everything is accomplished by the gift of food, O brahmin; there is no doubt. (40)
In ancient times, the twice-born Satyaketu, merely by giving food,
obtained the fruit of all merits and attained hard-to-reach liberation. (41)
Devoted to the Kārtika observance, one should give an excellent cow.
The observance reaches completeness through the gift of a cow; there is no doubt. (42)
Higher than the gift of a cow, ferry across the ocean of transmigration,
there is no [gift] in this world, O Nārada, as with the brahmin Suśarman. (43)
Even after bestowing numerous gifts in the month of Kārtika, O best of brahmins,

I am unable to describe the greatness of chanting the name,
just as the denizens of hell were formerly freed by Puṣkara. (45)
“Govinda, Govinda, Hari, Murāri, Govinda, Govinda, Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa,
Govinda, Govinda, who hold the chariot-wheel in hand, Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava!” (46)
Half a verse or a quarter of a verse from the Bhāgavata daily,
whoever recites in Kārtika, endowed with faith and devotion, [attains the highest state]. (47)
By those who have not heard the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, nor worshipped the ancient Puruṣa,
nor offered into the mouths of the earthly gods, the lives of those men have passed in vain. (48)
Whoever recites the Gītā in the month of Kārtika, O best of brahmins,
I have no power to describe the fruit of his merit. (49)
A scripture equal to the Gītā has never existed, nor will there ever be.
Taking away all sins eternally, the Gītā alone bestows liberation. (50)

the limit of his merit has not been defined by Viṣṇu. (52)
Having worshipped a śālagrāma, O great sage, to a learned brahmin
whoever gives it, O brahmin, hear the fruit of his merit! (53)
Whatever fruit comes from the gift of land extending to the seven oceans,
that fruit one attains through the gift of a śālagrāma stone. (54)
By the gift of a śālagrāma stone in Kārtika, just as a brahmin woman,
though a widow, became one whose husband is alive on the fifth day of marriage. (55)
Therefore, in the month of Kārtika, preceded by ablutions and gifts,
the gift of a śālagrāma stone should be performed; there is no doubt in this. (56)
Thus in the glorious Skanda Purāṇa, in the compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses], in the second Vaiṣṇava section, in the Greatness of the Month of Kārtika, the second chapter named “Description of the Rules of the Kārtika Observance.” (2)

कर्मणा मनसा वाचा पापमेभिः कदाचन .. न कृतं शिष्यवर्यैस्तैर्भवद्भिर्लोकनिष्ठुरैः .. वृथा संघातितास्ते तु कालमृत्युर्न चागतः .. तस्मान्न दोषो युष्माकं न चैषामपि पन्नगाः .. कर्तेषां यम एवाऽत्र यमं तस्माच्छपाम्यहम्.. इत्युक्त्वा जलमादाय यमं शप्तुं समुद्यतः ..” इति . तदा यमः सहसैव तत्रागत्योवाच-हे ऋषे . एषामकालमरणं न किंतु सर्पदंशनिमित्तेन महामृत्युकाल एवोपस्थितस्तस्माद्विचार्य शापं देहि नात्र ममापराधः . तदा गौतम उवाच-एवं सति एतैः सच्छिष्यैर्विना मम जीवितेन किं प्रयोजनम्, अतः मया यत्पुण्यमुपार्जितं यच्च तपस्तप्तं तेन पुण्येन तव कृपया च एते जीवनं प्राप्नुवंतु, एवमुक्ते ते सहसोत्थाय संहृष्टा अग्रतः गुरुं यमं च दृष्ट्वा ववंदिरे, गौतमः प्रीत्या तानालिंग्यातितुष्टः युष्माकं वरं दास्यामीत्युवाच-ऽसर्वान्वेदांश्च शास्त्राणि समस्तांगानि सुव्रताः .. इतिहासपुराणानि मत्प्रसादादवाप्स्यथ .. गुरुणैवं वरे दत्ते सेंद्रो गुरुरगात्ततः .. गौतमं प्रेतराजं च तांश्च विप्रानुवाच ह .. इन्द्रोहमस्मि भद्रं वः शृणुध्वं वचनं मम .. एतैर्द्विजैरतीवेह जिता लोकाश्च सर्वशः .. मम लोकमितस्तस्माद्गंतुमर्हथ सुव्रताः .. गौतमस्य प्रसादेन सदेहा एव गच्छत .. सामर्थ्यमेषां लोके च तव कीर्तिस्तथा मम .. कीर्तिश्च लोके ख्याता स्याद्गुरुपूजाफलं तथा.." इत्युक्त्वा तान्विमाने चा'ऽरोप्य दिवं ययौ, यमः स्वपुरं गौतमश्च स्वाश्रमं ययाविति ..
2.4.m:
2.4.2.8
To show that one obtains everything through the grace born of service to the guru, he states an illustrative story: Gautama had three disciples—Medhāvin, Kapila, and Sumati. Through excellent service to their guru, they attained divinity. Here is the famous story recounted in the Kārtikamāhātmya of the Sāroddhāra: Formerly, on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī at Siddhāśrama, the seer Gautama had three disciples: Medhāvin, Kapila, and Sumati. From their very childhood, they were dedicated to serving the guru. Once, Gautama called them and said: “O disciples, go quickly to the forest and bring kindling, flowers, fruits, and kuśa grass.” Having gathered only a few fruits and other items, they returned to their guru at midday. Gautama then became exceedingly angry and said: “O disciples, you went in the early morning, and now it is midday! You have brought very little fruit and the like; what, then, have you been doing for so long? O ill-behaved ones, if you wish to live, go back to the forest, gather many fruits and the like, and return quickly!” Hearing this, terrified, with throats withered by hunger, they went to the forest once again. There, wandering from forest to forest facing the west, afflicted with thirst, they bathed in a lake, performed the twilight devotion, drank water, and, while gathering fruits and the like, entered a terrifying forest. Night fell upon them. The roar of lions, tigers, and other beasts arose. Then, terrified, they said to one another: “Alas, how dreadful! In this deep dark forest we cannot see fruits or anything; we do not know the directions. Taking what shall we return to the guru's presence? What will become of us?” Distressed by fear and wandering here and there, they fell into a well overgrown with grass and bushes. There, bitten by serpents, they met their death. Gautama, realizing they had not returned and severely reproaching himself, went searching for them in the forest in the morning with his wife; seeing them dead in a well, he lamented. Then all [the serpents] consoled Gautama, saying: “They died solely through their own sin; why should you grieve?” Gautama said: / “Never did these best of disciples commit any sin / by action, mind, or speech. Cruel beings of this world that you are, / you struck them down in vain, for their allotted time of death had not arrived. / Therefore, the fault is not yours, nor is it that of these serpents; / the one who did this is Yama alone; hence, I shall curse Yama!” Saying this, taking water, he was about to curse Yama. Then Yama immediately arrived there and said: “O seer, this was not an untimely death for them; rather, the appointed time of great death arrived by reason of the serpent bites. Therefore, deliberate before issuing a curse; herein there is no fault of mine.” Gautama then said: “If this is so, what purpose have I in living without these good disciples? Therefore, by whatever merit I have earned and whatever austerity I have performed, through that merit and by your grace, let them attain life!” When this was said, they suddenly arose rejoicing, saw their guru and Yama before them, and bowed to them. Gautama embraced them with love and, exceedingly pleased, said, “I shall grant you a boon: / 'O men of good vows, through my grace you shall obtain / all the Vedas, the scriptures, all the auxiliary limbs, the epics, and the Purāṇas!' / When the guru had thus granted the boon, Indra arrived there with his preceptor. / He said to Gautama, the King of the Departed, and those brahmins: / 'I am Indra; may good betide you; hear my words! / By these twice-born men, indeed, all worlds have been completely conquered. / Therefore, O men of good vows, you ought to go from here to my world! / By the grace of Gautama, go in your very bodies! / Thus let their power be renowned in the world, as well as your renown and mine, / and also the fruit of honoring the guru!'” Having said this, he placed them on an aerial chariot and went to heaven; Yama went to his own city, and Gautama went to his own hermitage.

श्वेतः श्वेतनृपः पुष्करार्चनयोगेन कमलपूजनेन मुक्तिं प्राप .. अत्र प्रसिद्धा कथा ब्राह्मे - पुरा काश्मीरदेशे श्वेतोनाम नृपः इष्टापूर्तकर्मनिष्ठः महावैष्णवः राज्ये पुत्रमभिषिच्य पुष्करक्षेत्रं गत्वा अतितीव्रेण तपसा स्वशरीरं शोषयन्नस्तोत् स्तुत्यंते स्वदेहान्निर्गतं महाभयंकरं पुरुषं दृष्ट्वा त्वं कोऽसि कुत आगतोऽसीत्यपृच्छत्, तदा व्याध उवाच - हे राजन् त्वं पूर्वजन्मनि जनस्थानीयो नृपः मृगयायां मृगरूपधरं मुनिं हतवान् तेन ब्रह्महा जातः, एकदा रात्रौ ब्रह्महत्याभयान्मुक्तो भवामीति विचिंत्य परमभक्त्या कार्तिके कमलैविष्णुं पूजयामासिथ, तदैव उदरव्याधितः कंठगतेन प्राणेन नारायणीनाम्नीं स्वपत्नीं संस्मरन्मृतः, तेन पुण्येन त्वं स्वर्गं गतः, अहमपि स्वेन तेजमा कल्पपर्यंतं तत्र तव निकटे स्थितः, ततः कल्पांते इदानीं स त्वं काश्मीरदेशे सुमनसः राज्ञः गृहे श्वेतनाम्ना जातः, अत्रापि विष्णोराराधनस्तोत्रपाठेन त्वं शुद्धः . अतः व्याधरूपेण तव देहादहं निर्गतः, शुद्धश्च जातः, तच्छ्रुत्वा विस्मितो राजा व्याधमुवाच, हे व्याध यतस्त्वया मम जन्मांतरं स्मारितं तस्मान्मत्प्रसादेन त्वं धर्मव्याधो भविष्यसि, इत्युक्त्वा विमानमारुह्य परं स्थानमवाप, तस्मात्-"सहस्रकमलैः पूजा कार्तिके मधुसूदने . न तेषां पुनरावृत्तिः कल्पकोटिशतैरपि” इति ..
2.4.m:
2.4.2.12
The fruit of giving away a maiden in marriage is stated:
“An eight-year-old girl is Gaurī, and a nine-year-old is Rohiṇī; / a ten-year-old is a kanyā, and beyond that she has attained menses. / One who gives a Gaurī goes to the world of Brahmā; a Rohiṇī, to the world of the Sun; / a kanyā, to the heavenly world; a menstruating girl, to the world of Yama. / And for as many hairs as there are on the maiden's body, O son, / for that many thousands of years one is honored in the world of Rudra.”

2.4.2.32
Śveta, King Śveta, attained liberation through the practice of worshiping at Puṣkara, through the worship with lotuses. Here is the famous story in the Brahma Purāṇa: Formerly in the land of Kaśmīra, there was a king named Śveta, dedicated to sacrifices and charitable deeds, a great devotee of Viṣṇu. Having consecrated his son to the kingdom, he went to the sacred field of Puṣkara, and, drying up his body through exceedingly fierce austerity, he praised [the Lord]. At the end of his hymn of praise, seeing a terrifying man issue from his body, he asked: “Who are you, and whence have you come?” Then the hunter said: “O king, in a previous birth you were a king of Janasthāna. While hunting, you killed a sage who had assumed the form of a deer; thereby you became the slayer of a brahmin. Once at night, thinking 'May I be liberated from the fear of slaying a brahmin,' with supreme devotion you worshiped Viṣṇu with lotuses in the month of Kārtika. At that very time, suffering from an abdominal disease, with your life-breath rising to the throat, remembering your wife named Nārāyaṇī, you died. Through that merit you went to heaven; and I too, by my own radiance, remained near you there until the end of the cosmic age. Then, at the end of the cosmic age, you were born just now in the land of Kaśmīra in the house of King Sumanas, under the name of Śveta. Here also, through the recitation of the hymn of worship of Viṣṇu, you have been purified. Therefore, in the form of a hunter, I have issued from your body and have become pure.” Hearing that, the king, filled with astonishment, said to the hunter: “O hunter, since my previous birth has been recalled by you, through my grace you shall become Dharmavyādha.” Saying this, ascending an aerial chariot, he reached the supreme abode. Therefore:
“For those who perform worship of the slayer of Madhu with a thousand lotuses in Kārtika, / there is no return, even after hundreds of crores of cosmic ages.”

2.4.s:
2.4.2.41
satyaketuviṣaye kathāmāha sāroddhāre-purā satyajinnāmā brāhmaṇaḥ dharmaśīlaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yo niḥspṛhaḥ sadā tīrthayātrāparaḥ - "nānyeṣu ramate cittaṃ gaṃgāṃ nityaṃ smaratyasau .. bhāgīrathīṃ suniṣṇāto viśeṣeṇa mahāmuniḥ ..” sa tīrthayātrāṃ kurvannekadā viśālānagarīṃ gatvā janairdarśitaṃ satyaketugṛhaṃ praviveśa, tadā satyaketuḥ tṛṭparītaṃ kṣudhāviṣṭaṃ bhojanamicchaṃtaṃ satyajitaṃ dṛṣṭvā utthāya arghapādyapūjāṃ kṛtvovāca-he dvijottama tavāgamanenā'dya mama janmanaḥ sāphalyaṃ jātam . pitarastṛptāḥ, devāśca suprītā jātāḥ, he dvijendra icchitaṃ bhojanaṃ kuru, tvayi bhukte me kiṃcitkartavyaṃ nāvaśiṣyate, tava darśanādaprāpyaṃ na hi vidyate, tadā satyajiduvāca - he satyaketo tava śuśrūṣayā vākyena ca tṛpto'smi . kiṃ ca, annadātāraḥ loke bahavaḥ saṃti tatra tvayā sadṛśaḥ kopi na dṛṣṭaḥ tvaṃ gṛhasthāśramiṇāṃ madhye śreṣṭho'si . tvayā gaṃgāyātrā kṛtā na vā, tadā satyaketuruvāca - he dvija, madgṛhe atithīnāmannadātā anyaḥ ko'pi nāsti tenā'dyāpi bhāgīrathīsnānaṃ na jātaṃ tacchrutvā satyajitaṃ viniṃdastvayā bhāgīrathīsnānaṃ na kṛtam ataḥ tvadgṛhe'dya na bhokṣyāmītyuktvā gṛhānnirgatya snānārthaṃ bhāgīrathīṃ gataḥ, tadaiva gaṃgā aṃtarhitā'bhavata, sa yadā jalaṃ nāpaśyattadā kṛtāṃjalirgaṃgāṃ tuṣṭāva, he devi mayā aṇumātro'pyaparādho na kṛtaḥ, me darśanaṃ dehi, anyāyaṃ kṣaṃtumarhasi, iti stutā gaṃgā pratyakṣamūrtyā dvijamāha--he satyajit tvaṃ satyaketugṛhaṃ gatvā taṃ prasādya annaṃ bhuktvā punarāgaccha tadannabhojanena bahavo mokṣaṃ gatāḥ, iti gaṃgāvacaḥ śrutvā satyaketugṛhe bhojanaṃ kṛtvā, tadanujñātaḥ gaṃgāmāgataḥ gaṃgāṃ dṛṣṭvā snānaṃ cakāra evaṃ satyaketuḥ kevalamannadānapuṇyena sadgatiṃ prāpa iti .
2.4.2.43
kaścitsuśarmānāma brāhmaṇaḥ vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ śāṃto jiteṃdriyaḥ sarvayajñakartā dhanī nityadānaparaḥ sarveṣāṃ hite rataḥ purāṇavaktā baṃdhūnāṃ hitakṛt bahuputravān āsīt, sa ca uttare vayasi gṛhabhāraṃ putreṣu samarpya vanaṃ gatvā śrīviṣṇumārādhayan svīyatapasā svargaṃ prāpa, tatraikadā yamadūtaiḥ parājitāndevadūtānprati iṃdraḥ provāca-he dūtāḥ dharmiṣṭhāḥ, mamā''jñayā divaṃ yāṃtu pāpiṣṭhāḥ narakaṃ yāṃtu tatrāpi ye gopradātāraḥ te pāpino'pi divaṃ yāṃtu, godānena pāparāśirnaśyati, etadiṃdravacaḥ śrutvā suśarmā brāhmaṇaḥ svaputrānupadeṣṭumaṃtarikṣamārgeṇa putrānsaṃbodhya provāca - he putrāḥ yūyaṃ yadi svargamīpsatha tadā madvākyādgodānaṃ kartavyaṃ, godānātparamanyaddānaṃ triloke nāstīti uktvā gataḥ, te putrāśca aśarīravācaṃ śrutvā vismitāḥ saṃtaḥ sarve'pi vidhinā gopradānaṃ cakruḥ, tena sadgatiṃ prāptāḥ .
2.4.d:
2.4.2.41
सत्यकेतुविषये कथामाह सारोद्धारे-पुरा सत्यजिन्नामा ब्राह्मणः धर्मशीलः सर्वकामेभ्यो यो निःस्पृहः सदा तीर्थयात्रापरः - "नान्येषु रमते चित्तं गंगां नित्यं स्मरत्यसौ .. भागीरथीं सुनिष्णातो विशेषेण महामुनिः ..” स तीर्थयात्रां कुर्वन्नेकदा विशालानगरीं गत्वा जनैर्दर्शितं सत्यकेतुगृहं प्रविवेश, तदा सत्यकेतुः तृट्परीतं क्षुधाविष्टं भोजनमिच्छंतं सत्यजितं दृष्ट्वा उत्थाय अर्घपाद्यपूजां कृत्वोवाच-हे द्विजोत्तम तवागमनेनाऽद्य मम जन्मनः साफल्यं जातम् . पितरस्तृप्ताः, देवाश्च सुप्रीता जाताः, हे द्विजेन्द्र इच्छितं भोजनं कुरु, त्वयि भुक्ते मे किंचित्कर्तव्यं नावशिष्यते, तव दर्शनादप्राप्यं न हि विद्यते, तदा सत्यजिदुवाच - हे सत्यकेतो तव शुश्रूषया वाक्येन च तृप्तोऽस्मि . किं च, अन्नदातारः लोके बहवः संति तत्र त्वया सदृशः कोपि न दृष्टः त्वं गृहस्थाश्रमिणां मध्ये श्रेष्ठोऽसि . त्वया गंगायात्रा कृता न वा, तदा सत्यकेतुरुवाच - हे द्विज, मद्गृहे अतिथीनामन्नदाता अन्यः कोऽपि नास्ति तेनाऽद्यापि भागीरथीस्नानं न जातं तच्छ्रुत्वा सत्यजितं विनिंदस्त्वया भागीरथीस्नानं न कृतम् अतः त्वद्गृहेऽद्य न भोक्ष्यामीत्युक्त्वा गृहान्निर्गत्य स्नानार्थं भागीरथीं गतः, तदैव गंगा अंतर्हिताऽभवत, स यदा जलं नापश्यत्तदा कृतांजलिर्गंगां तुष्टाव, हे देवि मया अणुमात्रोऽप्यपराधो न कृतः, मे दर्शनं देहि, अन्यायं क्षंतुमर्हसि, इति स्तुता गंगा प्रत्यक्षमूर्त्या द्विजमाह--हे सत्यजित् त्वं सत्यकेतुगृहं गत्वा तं प्रसाद्य अन्नं भुक्त्वा पुनरागच्छ तदन्नभोजनेन बहवो मोक्षं गताः, इति गंगावचः श्रुत्वा सत्यकेतुगृहे भोजनं कृत्वा, तदनुज्ञातः गंगामागतः गंगां दृष्ट्वा स्नानं चकार एवं सत्यकेतुः केवलमन्नदानपुण्येन सद्गतिं प्राप इति .
2.4.2.43
कश्चित्सुशर्मानाम ब्राह्मणः वेदवेदांगपारगः शांतो जितेंद्रियः सर्वयज्ञकर्ता धनी नित्यदानपरः सर्वेषां हिते रतः पुराणवक्ता बंधूनां हितकृत् बहुपुत्रवान् आसीत्, स च उत्तरे वयसि गृहभारं पुत्रेषु समर्प्य वनं गत्वा श्रीविष्णुमाराधयन् स्वीयतपसा स्वर्गं प्राप, तत्रैकदा यमदूतैः पराजितान्देवदूतान्प्रति इंद्रः प्रोवाच-हे दूताः धर्मिष्ठाः, ममा'ऽज्ञया दिवं यांतु पापिष्ठाः नरकं यांतु तत्रापि ये गोप्रदातारः ते पापिनोऽपि दिवं यांतु, गोदानेन पापराशिर्नश्यति, एतदिंद्रवचः श्रुत्वा सुशर्मा ब्राह्मणः स्वपुत्रानुपदेष्टुमंतरिक्षमार्गेण पुत्रान्संबोध्य प्रोवाच - हे पुत्राः यूयं यदि स्वर्गमीप्सथ तदा मद्वाक्याद्गोदानं कर्तव्यं, गोदानात्परमन्यद्दानं त्रिलोके नास्तीति उक्त्वा गतः, ते पुत्राश्च अशरीरवाचं श्रुत्वा विस्मिताः संतः सर्वेऽपि विधिना गोप्रदानं चक्रुः, तेन सद्गतिं प्राप्ताः .
2.4.m:
2.4.2.41
Regarding Satyaketu, the story is related in the Sāroddhāra: Formerly there was a brahmin named Satyajit, virtuous, free from all desires, and always devoted to pilgrimage: "His mind delights in nothing else; he continually remembers the Gaṅgā. / Highly proficient regarding the Bhāgīrathī, especially so was that great sage." Making pilgrimages, he once went to the city of Viśālā and entered the house of Satyaketu, pointed out by the people. Then Satyaketu, seeing Satyajit afflicted with thirst, seized by hunger, and desiring food, stood up, performed the worship with offering of argha and pādhya, and said: "O best of the twice-born, by your arrival today the purpose of my life has been achieved. The ancestors are satisfied, and the gods have become well pleased. O king among the twice-born, eat the food you desire. When you have eaten, there remains nothing left for me to do; from your darśana there is indeed nothing unattainable." Then Satyajit said: "O Satyaketu, by your service and your words I am satisfied. Moreover, there are many givers of food in the world, yet none has been seen equal to you; you are the best among householders. Have you made a pilgrimage to the Gaṅgā or not?" Then Satyaketu said: "O twice-born, in my house there is no other giver of food to guests; therefore even to this day a ritual ablution in the Bhāgīrathī has not taken place." Hearing that, [Satyajit] censured him: "You have not performed a ritual ablution in the Bhāgīrathī; therefore I will not eat in your house today." Having spoken thus, he left the house and went to the Bhāgīrathī for a ritual ablution. At that very moment the Gaṅgā vanished. When he did not see the water, he folded his hands and praised the Gaṅgā: "O goddess, I have not committed even an atom of offense; grant me your darśana, you ought to forgive any wrongdoing." Praised thus, the Gaṅgā spoke to the twice-born in visible form: "O Satyajit, go to the house of Satyaketu, propitiate him, eat his food, and come back. By eating his food many have attained liberation." Hearing this speech of the Gaṅgā, he ate in the house of Satyaketu, and, permitted by him, came to the Gaṅgā, saw the Gaṅgā, and took his ritual ablution. Thus Satyaketu attained the good state solely through the religious merit of giving food.
2.4.2.43
There was a certain brahmin named Suśarman, a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, calm, with senses subdued, a performer of all sacrifices, wealthy, constantly devoted to charity, engaged in the welfare of all, an expounder of the Purāṇas, a benefactor to his kin, and having many sons. In his later years, having entrusted the household burden to his sons, he went to the forest, worshipped Lord Viṣṇu, and by his own austerity reached heaven. There once Indra said to the messengers of the gods who had been defeated by the messengers of Yama: "O messengers, let the righteous go to heaven by my command; let the most sinful go to hell. Even among them, let those who are givers of cows go to heaven though they be sinners; by the gift of a cow a heap of sin is destroyed." Hearing these words of Indra, the brahmin Suśarman, in order to instruct his own sons, addressed his sons through the celestial path and said: "O sons, if you desire heaven, then by my word the gift of a cow must be made; in the three worlds there is no gift higher than the gift of a cow." Having said this, he departed. And his sons, hearing the bodiless voice, were astonished, and all gave cows according to rule; thereby they attained the good state.

2.4.s:
2.4.2.45
puṣkaraviṣaye prasiddhā kathā sāroddhāre - purā naṃdigrāme puṣkaranāmānau dvau brāhmaṇau nivasataḥ tatraikaḥ puṇyātmā, aparaḥ pāpī, athaikadā yamaḥ pāpipuṣkarānayane dūtānājñāpayata, te ca taṃ vihāya puṇyavaṃtaṃ puṣkaramānītavaṃtaḥ, tadā yamaḥ dūtānnirbhartsya bahusaṃmānapūrvakaṃ puṣkaramuvāca-he puṣkara tavā''nayane mamājñā na tvaṃ punargaccha tadā puṣkara uvāca-he yama ahaṃ narakāndraṣṭumicchāmi, yatra pāpibhiryātanā anubhūyaṃte, tato yamadarśitaṃ hāhākāraravākulamatiduḥkhitaṃ nārakīyagaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā'tisaṃtrasto dayāparaḥ puṣkarastānuvāca--he nārakāḥ pūrvaṃ kimapi na vicāritam adhunā hāhākāreṇa kiṃ prayojanaṃ sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ bhagavannāmāpi na gṛhītam. nārakā ūcuḥ-he puṣkara tvayoktaṃ satyaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭha tavāṃgasparśavāyunā'smākaṃ sukhaṃ bhaviṣyati, tadā etaiḥ kiṃ prayojanaṃ tvaṃ gaccheti yamenoktaḥ puṣkara uvāca-he yama etānamocayitvā'haṃ gaṃtu notsahe ato mayā sarvabhūtātmā bhagavāngoviṃda ārādhitaścettena puṇyena ete nārakā muktā bhavaṃtu evamuktvā goviṃdagoviṃdeti viṣṇornāmasmaraṇamakarot . tadaiva sarve nārakāḥ muktāḥ divyarūpadharāḥ tava kīrtiratulā bhaviṣyatīti puṣkaramuktavaṃto vaikuṃṭhaṃ yayuḥ, puṣkaro'pi yamamāmaṃtrya nāmamahimnaiva paraṃ padaṃ gatavāniti ..45..
2.4.d:
2.4.2.45
पुष्करविषये प्रसिद्धा कथा सारोद्धारे - पुरा नंदिग्रामे पुष्करनामानौ द्वौ ब्राह्मणौ निवसतः तत्रैकः पुण्यात्मा, अपरः पापी, अथैकदा यमः पापिपुष्करानयने दूतानाज्ञापयत, ते च तं विहाय पुण्यवंतं पुष्करमानीतवंतः, तदा यमः दूतान्निर्भर्त्स्य बहुसंमानपूर्वकं पुष्करमुवाच-हे पुष्कर तवा'ऽनयने ममाज्ञा न त्वं पुनर्गच्छ तदा पुष्कर उवाच-हे यम अहं नरकान्द्रष्टुमिच्छामि, यत्र पापिभिर्यातना अनुभूयंते, ततो यमदर्शितं हाहाकाररवाकुलमतिदुःखितं नारकीयगणं दृष्ट्वाऽतिसंत्रस्तो दयापरः पुष्करस्तानुवाच--हे नारकाः पूर्वं किमपि न विचारितम् अधुना हाहाकारेण किं प्रयोजनं सर्वपापक्षयकरं भगवन्नामापि न गृहीतम्. नारका ऊचुः-हे पुष्कर त्वयोक्तं सत्यं क्षणं तिष्ठ तवांगस्पर्शवायुनाऽस्माकं सुखं भविष्यति, तदा एतैः किं प्रयोजनं त्वं गच्छेति यमेनोक्तः पुष्कर उवाच-हे यम एतानमोचयित्वाऽहं गंतु नोत्सहे अतो मया सर्वभूतात्मा भगवान्गोविंद आराधितश्चेत्तेन पुण्येन एते नारका मुक्ता भवंतु एवमुक्त्वा गोविंदगोविंदेति विष्णोर्नामस्मरणमकरोत् . तदैव सर्वे नारकाः मुक्ताः दिव्यरूपधराः तव कीर्तिरतुला भविष्यतीति पुष्करमुक्तवंतो वैकुंठं ययुः, पुष्करोऽपि यममामंत्र्य नाममहिम्नैव परं पदं गतवानिति ..45..
2.4.m:
2.4.2.45
Regarding Puṣkara, the renowned story is told in the Sāroddhāra: Formerly in the village of Nandigrāma there lived two brahmins named Puṣkara. Among them one was a virtuous soul and the other a sinner. Then once Yama ordered his messengers to bring the sinful Puṣkara. But they, leaving him aside, brought the virtuous Puṣkara. Then Yama, having reprimanded the messengers, with great respect said to Puṣkara: "O Puṣkara, my command was not for your bringing; go back again." Then Puṣkara said: "O Yama, I wish to see the hells where torments are experienced by sinners." Then, having seen the host of hell-dwellers shown by Yama, agitated by cries of distress and exceedingly miserable, Puṣkara, filled with great terror and moved by compassion, said to them: "O hell-dwellers, previously you considered nothing; now what is the use of wailing? You did not even utter the name of the Lord, which destroys all sin." The hell-dwellers said: "O Puṣkara, what you have spoken is true. Stay for a moment; by the wind touching your body we shall have comfort." Then, spoken to by Yama: "What is the use of these [sinners]? Go!", Puṣkara said: "O Yama, without having freed them, I do not dare to leave; therefore, if the Lord Govinda, the Self of all beings, has been worshipped by me, then by that merit let these hell-dwellers be liberated!" Having spoken thus, he remembered the name of Viṣṇu, saying, "Govinda, Govinda!" At that very moment all the hell-dwellers were liberated, assumed divine forms, and saying to Puṣkara, "Your fame will be incomparable!", went to Vaikuṇṭha. Puṣkara too, bidding farewell to Yama, went to the highest abode solely through the greatness of the [divine] Name. ..45..

2.4.s:
2.4.2.51
yathā jaḍonāma brāhmaṇaḥ gītādhyāyaśravaṇena mukto'bhūt . atra prasiddhā kathā sāroddhāre-vidarbhanagare kauśikānvayaḥ jaḍonāma brāhmaṇaḥ svadharmaṃ vihāya parastrīgāmī, madyapaścauryakarmarataḥ āsīt .. sa ekadā uttaradiktaḥ cauryeṇā'tīva dhanaṃ gṛhītvā āgacchanmārge tarormūle caurairghātitaḥ, tatastatputraḥ pitaraṃ nityamanveṣayanvārtāmapi nopalabdhavān tataḥ pituḥ pāralaukikaṃ karma kartuṃ saṃbhārāngṛhītvā vārāṇasīṃ gaṃtumupacakra me, mārge saptāṣṭau nivāsānnītvā ekasmiṃstarormūle yatra pūrvaṃ pitā nihataḥ tatra saṃdhyāṃ kṛtvā gītāyāstṛtīyā'dhyāyaṃ jajāpa, tadaiva ghoraśabdaṃ śrutvā ākāśādutpataṃtaṃ
vimānavarasaṃsthitaṃ divyarūpavaraṃ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇamya vṛttāṃtamapṛcchat . sa ca pitā āha-he putra yadarthaṃ vārāṇasīṃ gaṃtavyaṃ, tatsarvamadya kṛtaṃ; tvaṃ kṛtakāryo'si nivartasya .. gītādhyāyapaṭhanena tvayā'haṃ mocitaḥ, kiṃca-he putra mama bhrātā anye madanvayāśca narakaṃ pratipedire, te sarve tvayā gītāpaṭhanapuṇyadānena mocitavyāḥ, ityutktvā āśiṣaṃ dattvā viṣṇupadaṃ yayau .. putro'pi kālena yamalokaṃ gatvā gītāpāṭhajaṃ puṇyaṃ dattvā nārakīyānmocayitvā svayamapi paraṃ padaṃ yayāviti .. 51 ..
2.4.d:
2.4.2.51
यथा जडोनाम ब्राह्मणः गीताध्यायश्रवणेन मुक्तोऽभूत् . अत्र प्रसिद्धा कथा सारोद्धारे-विदर्भनगरे कौशिकान्वयः जडोनाम ब्राह्मणः स्वधर्मं विहाय परस्त्रीगामी, मद्यपश्चौर्यकर्मरतः आसीत् .. स एकदा उत्तरदिक्तः चौर्येणाऽतीव धनं गृहीत्वा आगच्छन्मार्गे तरोर्मूले चौरैर्घातितः, ततस्तत्पुत्रः पितरं नित्यमन्वेषयन्वार्तामपि नोपलब्धवान् ततः पितुः पारलौकिकं कर्म कर्तुं संभारान्गृहीत्वा वाराणसीं गंतुमुपचक्र मे, मार्गे सप्ताष्टौ निवासान्नीत्वा एकस्मिंस्तरोर्मूले यत्र पूर्वं पिता निहतः तत्र संध्यां कृत्वा गीतायास्तृतीयाऽध्यायं जजाप, तदैव घोरशब्दं श्रुत्वा आकाशादुत्पतंतं
विमानवरसंस्थितं दिव्यरूपवरं पितरं दृष्ट्वा प्रणम्य वृत्तांतमपृच्छत् . स च पिता आह-हे पुत्र यदर्थं वाराणसीं गंतव्यं, तत्सर्वमद्य कृतं; त्वं कृतकार्योऽसि निवर्तस्य .. गीताध्यायपठनेन त्वयाऽहं मोचितः, किंच-हे पुत्र मम भ्राता अन्ये मदन्वयाश्च नरकं प्रतिपेदिरे, ते सर्वे त्वया गीतापठनपुण्यदानेन मोचितव्याः, इत्युत्क्त्वा आशिषं दत्त्वा विष्णुपदं ययौ .. पुत्रोऽपि कालेन यमलोकं गत्वा गीतापाठजं पुण्यं दत्त्वा नारकीयान्मोचयित्वा स्वयमपि परं पदं ययाविति .. 51 ..
2.4.m:
2.4.2.51
As a brahmin named Jaḍa was liberated by hearing a chapter of the Gītā. On this matter, there is a well-known story in the Sāroddhāra: In the city of Vidarbha, there was a brahmin of the Kauśika lineage named Jaḍa who, having abandoned his own duty, had relations with other men's wives, drank wine, and was addicted to theft. Once, after acquiring great wealth through theft from the northern region, while returning, he was killed by thieves at the foot of a tree on the path. Then his son, constantly searching for his father, received no news at all. Thereupon, taking supplies to perform the rites for his father's afterlife, he set out to go to Vārāṇasī. Spending seven or eight nights on the path, at the foot of the very tree where his father had previously been killed, having performed the twilight prayers, he recited the third chapter of the Gītā. At that very moment, hearing a terrible sound, he saw his father descending from the sky seated in an excellent aerial chariot, endowed with a divine form. Bowing, he asked him what had happened. And his father said: 'O son, that for the sake of which you had to go to Vārāṇasī has all been accomplished today; your purpose is fulfilled, return! You have liberated me by reciting the chapter of the Gītā. Moreover, O son, my brother and others of my family have fallen into hell; all of them must be liberated by you by giving the merit of reciting the Gītā.' Having said this and given his blessing, he went to the realm of Viṣṇu. The son too, in the course of time, went to the realm of Yama, granted the merit born of reciting the Gītā, liberated the denizens of hell, and himself went to the supreme abode. 51.

2.4.s:
2.4.2.52
atha kārtike śāligrāma śilādānapraśaṃsāmāha-śāligrāmeti .. yathā brāhmaṇī vivāhātpaṃcamadivase bhartṛmaraṇayogena vidhavā jātā, paraṃtu śāligrāmaśilādānena bhartā jīvanaṃ prāpa tena sadhavā jātā, atra prasiddhā kathā sāroddhāre-godātīre kaścidvaiśyaḥ mahāpāparataḥ durācāraḥ āsīta, sa kadācidṛṇagrāhiṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ khaḍgenāghātayat, tataḥ maraṇāṃte rauravanarake patitaḥ atha dharmacāronāma tatputraḥ pitrārjitaṃ dhanaṃ yajñadānavratajapatapaiṣṭāpūrtaparopakārādisanmārgeṇa vyayīcakāra, ekadā dharmacāravaiśyagṛhe lomaśamunirāgatya tvaṃ śāligrāmaśilādānapuṇyena pitaraṃ rauravānmocayetyupadideśa, tadā saḥ śilādānaṃ vyarthamiti matvā ṛṣivacanamanādṛtya tūṣṇī sthitaḥ kālena mamāra ca lomaśo'pi tūṣṇīṃ yayau, sa dharmacāravaiśyaḥ śilāyā anādarādvipravākyasya laṃghanānmanvaṃtaraṃ narakayātanāṃ bhuktvā karmaśeṣeṇā'nekapaśuyoniṃ bhuktvā strījanmāni ca bhuktvā ekādaśe janmani yājakabrāhmaṇasya kanyā abhavat, tadā pitā prāptayauvanāṃ kanyāṃ dṛṣṭvā samānakulagotrāya dattvā vivāhamakarot atha tadbhartā paṃcame'hani vamanarogataḥ mṛtaḥ, tadā yājakaḥ jāmātaraṃ mṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā jāmātā kena jīvediti kṣaṇamātraṃ vicārya kārtike śāligrāmasya dānaṃ jīvane kāraṇamiti matvā sulakṣaṇaṃ manoharaṃ śāligrāmaṃ putryā hastena viprāya dāpayāmāsa, tadā tatkṣaṇādeva patiḥ jīvanaṃ prāpaṃ, tataḥ tau daṃpatī cirakālaṃ cikrīḍatuḥ, kālāṃtare sā yājakasutā śālagrāmadānapuṇyena strījanmato vinirmuktā satī viṣṇuyaśonāmakabrāhmaṇajanma labdhvā prativarṣaṃ kārtike śāligrāmadānapuṇyena mokṣaṃ prāpeti .. 55 .. śilādānaprasaṃgena śilālakṣaṇamāha pādme-"cakrāṃkitaṃ hiraṇyāṃgaṃ raśmijālaṃ vinirdiśet .. suvarṇarekhābahulaṃ sphaṭika dyutiśobhitam .. atisnigdhā siddhikarī kṛṣṇā kīrtiṃ dadāti ca .. pāṃḍurā pāpadahanī pītā putraphalapradā .. nīlā prayacchate lakṣmīṃ raktā rogapradāyinī .. rūkṣā udvegajananī vakrā dāridryabhāginī .. ekaṃ sudarśanaṃ jñeyaṃ lakṣmīnārāyaṇaṃ dvayam .. tṛtīyaṃ cā'cyutaṃ vidyāccaturthaṃ tu janārdanam .. paṃcamaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca ṣaṣṭhaṃ pradyumnameva ca .. saṃkarṣaṇaṃ saptamaṃ ca aṣṭamaṃ puruṣottamam .. navamaṃ ca navavyūhaṃ daśamaṃ tu daśātmakam .. ekādaśaṃ cā'niruddhaṃ dvādaśaṃ dvādaśātmakam .. ata ūrdhvaṃ tu cakrāṇi dṛśyaṃte'naṃtasaṃjñake .. khaṃḍite truṭite bhagne śāligrāme na doṣabhāk ..” iti .
2.4.d:
2.4.2.52
अथ कार्तिके शालिग्राम शिलादानप्रशंसामाह-शालिग्रामेति .. यथा ब्राह्मणी विवाहात्पंचमदिवसे भर्तृमरणयोगेन विधवा जाता, परंतु शालिग्रामशिलादानेन भर्ता जीवनं प्राप तेन सधवा जाता, अत्र प्रसिद्धा कथा सारोद्धारे-गोदातीरे कश्चिद्वैश्यः महापापरतः दुराचारः आसीत, स कदाचिदृणग्राहिणं ब्राह्मणं खड्गेनाघातयत्, ततः मरणांते रौरवनरके पतितः अथ धर्मचारोनाम तत्पुत्रः पित्रार्जितं धनं यज्ञदानव्रतजपतपैष्टापूर्तपरोपकारादिसन्मार्गेण व्ययीचकार, एकदा धर्मचारवैश्यगृहे लोमशमुनिरागत्य त्वं शालिग्रामशिलादानपुण्येन पितरं रौरवान्मोचयेत्युपदिदेश, तदा सः शिलादानं व्यर्थमिति मत्वा ऋषिवचनमनादृत्य तूष्णी स्थितः कालेन ममार च लोमशोऽपि तूष्णीं ययौ, स धर्मचारवैश्यः शिलाया अनादराद्विप्रवाक्यस्य लंघनान्मन्वंतरं नरकयातनां भुक्त्वा कर्मशेषेणाऽनेकपशुयोनिं भुक्त्वा स्त्रीजन्मानि च भुक्त्वा एकादशे जन्मनि याजकब्राह्मणस्य कन्या अभवत्, तदा पिता प्राप्तयौवनां कन्यां दृष्ट्वा समानकुलगोत्राय दत्त्वा विवाहमकरोत् अथ तद्भर्ता पंचमेऽहनि वमनरोगतः मृतः, तदा याजकः जामातरं मृतं दृष्ट्वा जामाता केन जीवेदिति क्षणमात्रं विचार्य कार्तिके शालिग्रामस्य दानं जीवने कारणमिति मत्वा सुलक्षणं मनोहरं शालिग्रामं पुत्र्या हस्तेन विप्राय दापयामास, तदा तत्क्षणादेव पतिः जीवनं प्रापं, ततः तौ दंपती चिरकालं चिक्रीडतुः, कालांतरे सा याजकसुता शालग्रामदानपुण्येन स्त्रीजन्मतो विनिर्मुक्ता सती विष्णुयशोनामकब्राह्मणजन्म लब्ध्वा प्रतिवर्षं कार्तिके शालिग्रामदानपुण्येन मोक्षं प्रापेति .. 55 .. शिलादानप्रसंगेन शिलालक्षणमाह पाद्मे-"चक्रांकितं हिरण्यांगं रश्मिजालं विनिर्दिशेत् .. सुवर्णरेखाबहुलं स्फटिक द्युतिशोभितम् .. अतिस्निग्धा सिद्धिकरी कृष्णा कीर्तिं ददाति च .. पांडुरा पापदहनी पीता पुत्रफलप्रदा .. नीला प्रयच्छते लक्ष्मीं रक्ता रोगप्रदायिनी .. रूक्षा उद्वेगजननी वक्रा दारिद्र्यभागिनी .. एकं सुदर्शनं ज्ञेयं लक्ष्मीनारायणं द्वयम् .. तृतीयं चाऽच्युतं विद्याच्चतुर्थं तु जनार्दनम् .. पंचमं वासुदेवं च षष्ठं प्रद्युम्नमेव च .. संकर्षणं सप्तमं च अष्टमं पुरुषोत्तमम् .. नवमं च नवव्यूहं दशमं तु दशात्मकम् .. एकादशं चाऽनिरुद्धं द्वादशं द्वादशात्मकम् .. अत ऊर्ध्वं तु चक्राणि दृश्यंतेऽनंतसंज्ञके .. खंडिते त्रुटिते भग्ने शालिग्रामे न दोषभाक् ..” इति .
2.4.m:
2.4.2.52
Now he states the praise of the gift of a Śāligrāma stone in the month of Kārtika: 'śāligrāma...' As a brahmin woman became a widow due to the death of her husband on the fifth day after marriage, but through the gift of a Śāligrāma stone her husband regained life, whereby she became a woman whose husband was living. On this matter, there is a well-known story in the Sāroddhāra: On the bank of the Godā[varī], there was a certain vaiśya addicted to great sin and of vile conduct. Once he struck with a sword a brahmin who had taken a debt; therefore, at the end of his life, he fell into the Raurava hell. Now his son named Dharmacāra expended the wealth acquired by his father through the virtuous path of sacrifices, gifts, vows, recitations, austerities, public works, beneficence to others, and the like. Once the sage Lomaśa came to the house of the vaiśya Dharmacāra and instructed: 'Liberate your father from Raurava through the merit of gifting a Śāligrāma stone.' Then, thinking that the gift of a stone was useless and disregarding the seer's words, he remained silent; and in time, he died, while Lomaśa also departed in silence. That vaiśya Dharmacāra, from disrespecting the stone and disregarding the brahmin's words, suffered the torments of hell for a manvantara, experienced various animal wombs due to the residue of karma, and experienced births as a woman, and in the eleventh birth became the daughter of a priest-brahmin. Then the father, seeing his daughter arrived at youth, gave her in marriage to one of equal family and lineage. Then her husband died on the fifth day from a vomiting illness. Then the priest, seeing his son-in-law dead, reflecting for a moment, 'By what might the son-in-law live?', and thinking that a gift of a Śāligrāma in Kārtika was the cause for life, caused a handsome Śāligrāma with auspicious marks to be given to a brahmin through the hand of his daughter. Then at that very moment the husband regained life. Then the couple sported for a long time. In the course of time, that daughter of the priest, having become entirely freed from birth as a woman through the merit of gifting a Śāligrāma, and having attained birth as a brahmin named Viṣṇuyaśas, attained liberation every year in Kārtika through the merit of gifting a Śāligrāma. 55. In connection with the gift of the stone, he states the characteristics of the stone from the Padma Purāṇa: 'One should indicate [a stone] marked with discs, having gold in its body, with a network of rays, full of streaks of gold, adorned with the luster of crystal. / An extremely smooth one brings accomplishment, and a black one grants fame; / a pale one burns sins, a yellow one grants the fruit of sons; / a blue one bestows fortune, a red one produces disease; / a rough one generates agitation, a crooked one partakes of poverty. / One [disc] is to be known as Sudarśana; two as Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa; / one should know three as Acyuta, and four indeed as Janārdana; / the fifth as Vāsudeva, and the sixth as Pradyumna; / the seventh as Saṃkarṣaṇa, and the eighth as Puruṣottama; / the ninth as Navavyūha, and the tenth having the nature of ten; / the eleventh as Aniruddha, and the twelfth having the nature of twelve; / above that, discs seen [on a stone] are called Ananta. / When a Śāligrāma is fractured, cracked, or broken, it incurs no defect.'"

2.4.s:
2.4.2.55
yathā brāhmaṇī vivāhātpaṃcamadivase bhartṛmaraṇayogena vidhavā jātā, paraṃtu śāligrāmaśilādānena bhartā jīvanaṃ prāpa tena sadhavā jātā, atra prasiddhā kathā sāroddhāre - godātīre kaścidvaiśyaḥ mahāpāparataḥ durācāraḥ āsīt, sa kadācidṛṇagrāhiṇaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ khaḍgenāghātayat, tataḥ maraṇāṃte rauravanarake patitaḥ atha dharmacāronāma tatputraḥ pitrārjitaṃ dhanaṃ yajñadānavratajapatapaiṣṭāpūrtaparopakārādisanmārgeṇa vyayīcakāra, ekadā dharmacāravaiśyagṛhe lomaśamunirāgatya tvaṃ śāligrāmaśilādānapuṇyena pitaraṃ rauravānmocayetyupadideśa, tadā saḥ śilādānaṃ vyarthamiti matvā ṛṣivacanamanādṛtya tūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ kālena mamāra ca lomaśo'pi tūṣṇīṃ yayau, sa dharmacāravaiśyaḥ śilāyā anādarādvipravākyasya laṃghanānmanvaṃtaraṃ narakayātanāṃ bhuktvā karmaśeṣeṇā'nekapaśuyoniṃ bhuktvā strījanmāni ca bhuktvā ekādaśe janmani yājakabrāhmaṇasya kanyā abhavat, tadā pitā prāptayauvanāṃ kanyāṃ dṛṣṭvā samānakulagotrāya dattvā vivāhamakarot atha tadbhartā paṃcame'hani vamanarogataḥ mṛtaḥ, tadā yājakaḥ jāmātaraṃ mṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā jāmātā kena jīvaditi kṣaṇamātraṃ vicārya kārtike śāligrāmasya dānaṃ jīvane kāraṇamiti matvā sulakṣaṇaṃ manoharaṃ śāligrāmaṃ putryā hastena viprāya dāpayāmāsa, tadā tatkṣaṇādeva patiḥ jīvanaṃ prāpaṃ, tataḥ tau daṃpatī cirakālaṃ cikrīḍatuḥ, kālāṃtare sā yājakasutā śālagrāmadānapuṇyena strījanmato vinirmuktā satī viṣṇuyaśonāmakabrāhmaṇajanma labdhvā prativarṣaṃ kārtike śāligrāmadānapuṇyena mokṣaṃ prāpeti .. 55 ..
2.4.d:
2.4.2.55
यथा ब्राह्मणी विवाहात्पंचमदिवसे भर्तृमरणयोगेन विधवा जाता, परंतु शालिग्रामशिलादानेन भर्ता जीवनं प्राप तेन सधवा जाता, अत्र प्रसिद्धा कथा सारोद्धारे - गोदातीरे कश्चिद्वैश्यः महापापरतः दुराचारः आसीत्, स कदाचिदृणग्राहिणं ब्राह्मणं खड्गेनाघातयत्, ततः मरणांते रौरवनरके पतितः अथ धर्मचारोनाम तत्पुत्रः पित्रार्जितं धनं यज्ञदानव्रतजपतपैष्टापूर्तपरोपकारादिसन्मार्गेण व्ययीचकार, एकदा धर्मचारवैश्यगृहे लोमशमुनिरागत्य त्वं शालिग्रामशिलादानपुण्येन पितरं रौरवान्मोचयेत्युपदिदेश, तदा सः शिलादानं व्यर्थमिति मत्वा ऋषिवचनमनादृत्य तूष्णीं स्थितः कालेन ममार च लोमशोऽपि तूष्णीं ययौ, स धर्मचारवैश्यः शिलाया अनादराद्विप्रवाक्यस्य लंघनान्मन्वंतरं नरकयातनां भुक्त्वा कर्मशेषेणाऽनेकपशुयोनिं भुक्त्वा स्त्रीजन्मानि च भुक्त्वा एकादशे जन्मनि याजकब्राह्मणस्य कन्या अभवत्, तदा पिता प्राप्तयौवनां कन्यां दृष्ट्वा समानकुलगोत्राय दत्त्वा विवाहमकरोत् अथ तद्भर्ता पंचमेऽहनि वमनरोगतः मृतः, तदा याजकः जामातरं मृतं दृष्ट्वा जामाता केन जीवदिति क्षणमात्रं विचार्य कार्तिके शालिग्रामस्य दानं जीवने कारणमिति मत्वा सुलक्षणं मनोहरं शालिग्रामं पुत्र्या हस्तेन विप्राय दापयामास, तदा तत्क्षणादेव पतिः जीवनं प्रापं, ततः तौ दंपती चिरकालं चिक्रीडतुः, कालांतरे सा याजकसुता शालग्रामदानपुण्येन स्त्रीजन्मतो विनिर्मुक्ता सती विष्णुयशोनामकब्राह्मणजन्म लब्ध्वा प्रतिवर्षं कार्तिके शालिग्रामदानपुण्येन मोक्षं प्रापेति .. 55 ..
2.4.m:
2.4.2.55
Just as a brahmin woman became a widow on the fifth day after her wedding through the death of her husband, yet through the gift of a śāligrāma stone her husband regained life and thereby she became one whose husband is alive. Here the well-known story in the Sāroddhāra is told: On the bank of the Godāvarī there was a certain vaiśya addicted to great sin and of vile conduct. Once he struck with a sword a brahmin who had taken a debt; therefore, at the end of his life, he fell into the Raurava hell. Then his son, named Dharmacāra, spent the wealth earned by his father on good paths such as sacrifices, gifts, vows, recitation, austerities, public works, and benevolence. Once the sage Lomaśa came to the house of the vaiśya Dharmacāra and instructed him: 'Through the religious merit of giving a śāligrāma stone, release your father from Raurava.' Then, thinking the gift of a stone to be useless and disregarding the ṛṣi's words, he remained silent, and in time he died; Lomaśa too departed silently. That vaiśya Dharmacāra, because of his disrespect for the stone and transgression of the sage's word, endured the torments of hell for a manvantara; by the residue of his karma, having passed through many animal wombs and female births, in his eleventh birth he became the daughter of a priest brahmin. Then the father, seeing his daughter having reached youth, gave her in marriage to one of equal lineage and family. Then her husband died on the fifth day of a vomiting illness. Then the priest, seeing his son-in-law dead, thought for a mere moment: 'By what means might the son-in-law live?' Considering that the gift of a śāligrāma in the month of Kārtika would be the cause of life, he caused a śāligrāma of auspicious marks and charming appearance to be given to a brahmin through the hand of his daughter. Then at that very moment the husband regained life; thereupon the couple sported for a long time. In the course of time, that priest's daughter, freed from female birth by the religious merit of gifting a śāligrāma and having obtained birth as a brahmin named Viṣṇuyaśas, attained liberation through the merit of gifting a śāligrāma every year in Kārtika. 55.

2.4.s:
2.4.2.56
śilādānaprasaṃgena śilālakṣaṇamāhapādme-"cakrāṃkitaṃ hiraṇyāṃgaṃ raśmijālaṃ vinirdiśet .. suvarṇarekhābahulaṃ sphāṭikadyutiśobhitam .. atisnigdhā siddhikarī kṛṣṇā kīrtiṃ dadāti ca .. pāṃḍurā pāpadahanī pītā putraphalapradā .. nīlā prayacchate lakṣmīṃ raktā rogapradāyinī .. rūkṣā udvegajananī vakrā dāridryabhāginī .. ekaṃ sudarśanaṃ jñeyaṃ lakṣmīnārāyaṇaṃ dvayam .. tṛtīyaṃ cā'cyutaṃ vidyāccaturthaṃ tu janārdanam .. paṃcamaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca ṣaṣṭhaṃ pradyumnameva ca .. saṃkarṣaṇaṃ saptamaṃ ca aṣṭamaṃ puruṣottamam .. navamaṃ ca navavyūhaṃ daśamaṃ tu daśātmakam .. ekādaśaṃ cā'niruddhaṃ dvādaśaṃ dvādaśātmakam .. ata ūrdhvaṃ tu cakrāṇi dṛśyate'naṃtasaṃjñake .. khaṃḍite truṭite bhagne śāligrāme na doṣabhāk ..” iti . evaṃ dāmodarādimūrtīnāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vartate graṃthavistarabhayānnocyate iti .. 56 ..
2.4.d:
2.4.2.56
शिलादानप्रसंगेन शिलालक्षणमाहपाद्मे-"चक्रांकितं हिरण्यांगं रश्मिजालं विनिर्दिशेत् .. सुवर्णरेखाबहुलं स्फाटिकद्युतिशोभितम् .. अतिस्निग्धा सिद्धिकरी कृष्णा कीर्तिं ददाति च .. पांडुरा पापदहनी पीता पुत्रफलप्रदा .. नीला प्रयच्छते लक्ष्मीं रक्ता रोगप्रदायिनी .. रूक्षा उद्वेगजननी वक्रा दारिद्र्यभागिनी .. एकं सुदर्शनं ज्ञेयं लक्ष्मीनारायणं द्वयम् .. तृतीयं चाऽच्युतं विद्याच्चतुर्थं तु जनार्दनम् .. पंचमं वासुदेवं च षष्ठं प्रद्युम्नमेव च .. संकर्षणं सप्तमं च अष्टमं पुरुषोत्तमम् .. नवमं च नवव्यूहं दशमं तु दशात्मकम् .. एकादशं चाऽनिरुद्धं द्वादशं द्वादशात्मकम् .. अत ऊर्ध्वं तु चक्राणि दृश्यतेऽनंतसंज्ञके .. खंडिते त्रुटिते भग्ने शालिग्रामे न दोषभाक् ..” इति . एवं दामोदरादिमूर्तीनां लक्षणं वर्तते ग्रंथविस्तरभयान्नोच्यते इति .. 56 ..
2.4.m:
2.4.2.56
In connection with the gift of the stone, the characteristics of the stone are stated in the Padma Purāṇa: 'One should indicate it as marked with a disc, having golden parts, and possessor of a net of rays; abundant in golden streaks, and beautified with the lustre of crystal. An extremely glossy one brings perfection, and a black one bestows renown; / a pale white one burns sins, a yellow one grants the fruit of sons; / a blue one bestows fortune, a red one gives disease; / a dry, rough one causes agitation, a crooked one brings poverty. One disc should be known as Sudarśana, two as Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa; / a third one should know as Acyuta, and a fourth as Janārdana; / the fifth as Vāsudeva, and the sixth as Pradyumna; / the seventh as Saṃkarṣaṇa, and the eighth as Puruṣottama; / the ninth as Navavyūha, and the tenth as Daśātman; / the eleventh as Aniruddha, and the twelfth as Dvādaśātman; / above that, when discs are seen, it is called Ananta. Even if chipped, broken, or cracked, a śāligrāma brings no fault.' Thus are the characteristics of the forms of Dāmodara and others, which are not stated here for fear of lengthening the text. 56.

पुरा प्रभंजनोनाम नृपः मृगयायां गुल्मांतरे स्थितां वत्सं पाययतीं मृगीं विव्याध, तदा मृगी उवाच-हे नृप तनयस्य स्तनं प्रयच्छंती त्वया हता . अतस्त्वं व्याघ्ररूपत्वमाप्नुहि . तदा शापेन त्रस्तो राजा प्रांजलिः सन्नुवाच-हे मृगि व्याघ्ररूपं मुक्त्वा मानुषं कदा प्राप्स्यामि, तद्वदामृग्युवाच-हे नृप, कार्तिके पुष्करे यदा नंदया सह तव संवादो भविष्यति तदा मुक्तो भविष्यति एवमुक्त्वा सा मृता, नृपोऽपि वर्षशतं व्याघ्ररूपेण वने .परिभ्रमन् कदा मुक्तिर्भविष्यतीति चितयन्नेकदा नंदानामिकां गां दृष्ट्वा खादितुमारेभे तदा नंदा अनेकविधसत्यप्रतिज्ञां कृत्वा वत्सं पाययित्वा पुनः व्याघ्रसमीपमागत्य अनेकविधधर्मभाषणेनोपदेशं चकार . तदा व्याघ्र उवाच-हे नंदः, अहं पूर्वं मृग्या शप्तः व्याघ्ररूपो जातः, परं त्वद्य त्वत्संपर्कोपदेशेन जातस्मरणः पुनर्नृपत्वमापन्नः, नाहं व्याघ्रः, एतस्मिन्नंतरे धर्मस्तत्रागत्य नंदामुवाच-हे नंदे त्वं नंदानाम सरस्वती नदी भविष्यसि, किंच ऊर्जे पुष्करे मासमात्रं स्नानं कुरु ततो मुक्तिर्भविष्यति इत्युक्त्वांऽतर्हितः . प्रभंजनोऽपि वसिष्ठोपेदेशेन कार्तिकसेवनान्मुक्तिं प्रापेति ..84 ..85.. इति कार्तिकमासमाहात्म्यटीकायां चतुर्थोऽध्यायः .. 4 ..
2.4.m:
2.4.4.84
Formerly, a king named Prabhañjana, while hunting, shot an arrow at a female deer suckling her fawn standing inside a bush. Then the female deer said: 'O king, you have struck me while I was offering the breast to my son. Therefore, attain the state of a tiger!' Then the king, frightened by the curse, with folded palms, said: 'O female deer, when shall I, having abandoned the form of a tiger, regain human form? Tell that!' The female deer said: 'O king, when in Kārtika at Puṣkara you have a conversation with Nandā, then you will be liberated.' Having spoken thus, she died. The king too, wandering in the forest for a hundred years in the form of a tiger, wondering when liberation would occur, once saw a cow named Nandā and began to devour her. Then Nandā, having made many kinds of oaths of truth and having suckled her calf, returned near the tiger and instructed him with many kinds of discourses on righteousness. Then the tiger said: 'O Nandā, I was previously cursed by a female deer and became a tiger. But today, through the instruction of your company, I have regained my memory and returned to kinghood; I am not a tiger.' In the meantime, Dharma came there and said to Nandā: 'O Nandā, you shall become the river Sarasvatī named Nandā. Moreover, in Kārtika at Puṣkara, bathe for merely a month; then liberation will occur.' Having spoken thus, he vanished. Prabhañjana also, by the instruction of Vasiṣṭha and by serving Kārtika, attained liberation. 84 85. Thus ends the fourth chapter in the commentary on the glorification of the month of Kārtika. 4

2.4.m: Brahmā said: / When two nāḍīs remain of the night, one should go to a reservoir of water, / bringing tulasī and clay, and carrying a water-pot with a cloth, O sage. (1) / Having arrived near the water and placed the pot on the bank, / having washed one's feet, one should recite the place, time, and so forth. (2) / One should remember the Gaṅgā and other rivers, and deities headed by Viṣṇu and Śarva. / Standing in navel-deep water, one should utter this mantra: (3) / 'In Kārtika, I shall perform the morning ritual ablution, O Janārdana, / for your pleasure, O Lord of gods, O Dāmodara, along with [you]. (4) / Having performed my regular and occasional duties in Kārtika, O destroyer of sin, / I shall offer a bath and water of oblation; make it free from obstacles, O Keśava.' (5) / And one should offer water of oblation and the rest in order to the deities of the sacred ford and others: / 'Accept the water of oblation offered by me together with Rādhā, O Hari! (6) / Homage to the lotus-naveled one! Homage to you who recline on the waters! / Homage be to you, Hṛṣīkeśa! Accept the water of oblation; homage be to you! (7) / For me, a practitioner of vows who have bathed according to the rule in the month of Kārtika, / accept the water of oblation offered by me, O slayer of the chief of Danujas! (8) / May Kiraṇā, Dhūtapāpā, and Sarasvatī of holy waters, / and Gaṅgā and Yamunā—the five rivers—purify me.' (9) / And one should offer water of oblation to other rivers according to the rule. / A man should make remembrance of Jāhnavī in all sacred fords; (10) / but at Jāhnavī, no other sacred ford should ever be remembered. / Having uttered these mantras, one should perform the bath for cleansing dirt; (11) / and then the bath with clay, the bath for the ancestors, and the bath for the guru. / Then one should sprinkle one's head with the Pāvamānī hymns. (12) / Having performed the Aghamarṣaṇa rite and the water-libation as an ancillary of the bath, / one should then sprinkle water on one's head with the Puruṣasūkta. (13) / Then, having come outside, one should place the water of the sacred ford upon one's head; / having sipped the holy water three times, taking a tulasī leaf in hand, (14) / then having stepped out of the water, one should wring out the hem [of the cloth] outside: (15cd)

2.4.m: 'Since the water was defiled by me with accumulations of bodily impurities, (15ab) / for the sake of removing that fault I make an offering to consumption.' / Having wrung out the cloth, one should apply the tilaka mark and the rest. (16) / Sūta said: / Listen, all you seers, to the fruit arising from the Kārtika ritual ablution, / which was spoken in detail by Sūrya to Aruṇa. (17) / Aruṇa said: / At which sacred ford or in which sacred field is the fruit arising in Kārtika / particularly [great] through conjunction with ritual ablution? Tell this, O Lord. (18) / Sūrya said: / Wherever it may be, the ritual ablution of Kārtika should be performed in water; / anywhere in Kārtika, a bath should be taken with hot water [if needed]; (19) / from that, the merit is tenfold through immersion in cold water; / a hundredfold greater than that is the merit obtained in the water of an outdoor well; (20) / the fruit is a thousandfold that of a well from pouring water from a step-well; / tenfold greater than that is the merit that arises from bathing in a pool; (21) / from that, the merit is tenfold through immersion in mountain streams; / far greater than that is the merit of river bathing in Kārtika; (22) / bathing at a sacred ford is said to be tenfold that of a river, O best of birds; / tenfold greater than that is the merit where there is a confluence of two rivers; (23) / at the confluence of three rivers there is no end to the merit. / The Sindhu, Kṛṣṇā, Veṇī, Yamunā, and Sarasvatī, (24) / Godāvarī, Vipāśā, Narmadā, Tamasā, Mahī, / Kāverī, Śarayū, Śiprā, and also the Carmaṇvatī river, (25) / Vitastā, Vedikā, Śoṇa, Vetravatī, Aparājitā, / Gaṇḍakī, Gomatī, Pūrṇā, Brahmaputrā, Sarovara, (26) / Vāgmatī, and Śatadru, and likewise Badarikāśrama— / these sacred fords are difficult to attain in Kārtika; now learn of them from me. (27) / Above all places, Āryāvarta is indeed the giver of merit; / Kolhāpurī is superior to that; after that, the two Kāñcīs are remembered, (28) / the abode of Anantasena, and also the Varāhakṣetra. 2.4.m: Cakrakṣetra is more meritorious than that, and Muktikṣetra is higher than that; / Avantikā is better than that, and Badarikāśrama is beyond that; / Ayodhyā is better than that, and Gaṅgādvāra is higher than that; / Kanakhala tīrtha is beyond that, and superior to that is Madhupurī. / Even for a single month of Kārtika in the waters of the Yamunā at Mathurā, / those who bathe indeed dwell in Vaikuṇṭha for a long time. / Rādhādāmodara himself bathed there in Kārtika; / therefore Madhupurī is supreme, and especially the Yamunā. / Dvārāvatī is even better than that; there Keśava bathes every day, / accompanied by sixteen thousand women together with the Yādavas. / The man who wears on his forehead a tilaka made from the clay of Dvārakā / is to be recognized as liberated while alive; there is no doubt. / The māhātmya of bathing at Dvārakā cannot be fully told by me; / for those whose minds are offered to Govinda, it shines like the sun of merit. / Superior to that is the Bhāgīrathī where she unites with the Vindhya; / ten times the merit of that arises here in the King of Tīrthas. / At the end of ten thousand [years] of the Kali age, Viṣṇu will abandon the earth; / at half that [time], the waters of Jāhnavī, and at half that [time], the hosts of deities. / As long as the Gaṅgā remains here, so long do the tīrthas exist, / and just so long do they take away the sin of men each in its own place. / When the Gaṅgā is lost, who indeed will take away that sin? / Considering thus, the excellent tīrthas will depart from the surface of the earth. / Therefore, O chief sages, as long as the Jāhnavī remains, / so long let dharma be practiced; thereafter let one withdraw into the earth, / having assumed a very firm samādhi, until the Kṛtayuga comes. / Otherwise, the wise man would be brought to ruin by the age of Kali. / Greater than that is Kāśī, of which no destruction takes place; / taking refuge in which, even the Gaṅgā washes away all sin. / There is no destruction of Kāśī even when Brahmā has died.

2.4.m: For the darśana of which even the Gaṅgā turned and flowed northwards. / In it is the tīrtha of Pañcanada, renowned in the three worlds. / When the month of Kārtika arrives, the ancestors who have gone to the Raurava hell / cry out: ‘In our lineage there will arise / someone, the foremost among the fortunate, who will go to auspicious Pañcanada / and perform an offering of water for us, delivering us from the ocean of hell!’ / When the month of Kārtika arrives, the King of Tīrthas and the other tīrthas / come to Pañcagaṅgā for ritual ablution; there is no doubt. / Even after committing a hundred thousand sins, by bathing at auspicious Pañcanada / and worshipping Bindumādhava, they instantly vanish. / For those who have bathed even once in auspicious Pañcanada during the month of Kārtika, / the fruit becomes ten million times that of bathing performed at all [other] tīrthas. / Brahmā said: / In the month of Kārtika, whoever desires to take a ritual ablution in the Kāverī, / by that alone is freed from sin and attains union with Viṣṇu. / Who could describe the supremely excellent māhātmya of the Kāverī? / In this regard, I shall narrate to you an ancient tale. / Listen with an attentive mind, O brahmin, regarding the Kāverī: / On the northern bank of the Gautamī is she who was born from the lotus-foot of Viṣṇu, / the Gaṅgā, destroyer of the sins of the three worlds, worshipped by the world. / Once, filled with misgivings about sin, that Gaṅgā reflected: / ‘All people come and cast their sin upon me; / but how will that sin go away?’ So, overcome with concern then, / she went to Kailāsa to ask Bhava, the beloved of the mountain’s daughter. / Beholding the great Rudra there, she who was born from Hari’s foot spoke: / Gaṅgā said: / O great Rudra, obeisance to you! I have come to ask you: / all people come and cast their sin upon me; / that sin cannot be endured by me, O husband of Pārvatī! / Tell me that means by which that sin may not come to me.

2.4.m: Hearing this speech of the Gaṅgā, the supreme Lord replied: / Rudra said: / In the beginning, for the eradication of sin, you emerged / from the lotus-foot of Padmanābha, O goddess! Why are you distressed? / Sovereignty over the destruction of sin was ordained for you by Viṣṇu. / Even so, I shall tell you the means for the eradication of sin. / The daughter of Kavi, the divine Kāverī, is the best of rivers; / and she is the most supreme of all through the force of Hari’s power. / In her lies the capacity for the destruction of all sins. / The man who performs ritual ablution in the Kāverī during the month of Kārtika / is freed from sin and goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / Therefore, go to her, O goddess; then you will be liberated from sin. / Thus addressed, she then went to the Kāverī, which removes sins. / By the mere touch of its water in Kārtika, she who was born from Viṣṇu’s foot, / her sins cleansed, the Gaṅgā went to her own abode. / Every year in Kārtika, with devotion the Gaṅgā comes to the Kāverī, / the purifier of the three worlds, which removes sin, in order to bathe. / By the mere touch of its water in Kārtika, she who was born from Viṣṇu’s foot, / her sins cleansed, the Gaṅgā went to her own abode. / Therefore, the Tulā ablution in the Kāverī is recommended and praised by the wise. / The one who performs the Tulā ablution in the Kāverī with devotion, O sage, / is immediately released from wickedness and then goes to the supreme state. / Therefore, bathing in the Kāverī in the month of Kārtika is praised. / Having heard this ancient tale, one devoted to the vow of Kārtika / obtains the fruit of bathing in the Kāverī and the supreme state. / Ablution at the close of night is supreme, pleasing to Viṣṇu; / at sunrise it is intermediate; as long as Kṛttikā has not set, / just so long is the ablution valid; otherwise, it is not of Kārtika. / Ablution must be performed by women having received the permission of their husband; / a religious act done without asking one’s husband leads to loss.

2.4.m: For women there is no other duty whatsoever apart from their husband. / She who follows the husband's command, even if she should commit a thousand sins, / is righteous in the world; she would not become so through vows and the like. / Even if the husband is poor, fallen, foolish, or wretched, / such a one is the refuge of women; from abandoning him, she would go to hell. / In the Kali [age], child, people show laxity in the rite of bathing. / Even so, I shall describe the bathing in Kārtika and Māgha. / He whose hands and feet, voice and mind are well controlled, / and who possesses learning, austerity, and renown, enjoys the fruit of sacred fords. / The faithless person, the sinful soul, the atheist, one of vacillating mind, / and the sophist—these five do not share in the fruit of sacred fords. / A brahmin who, having risen in the morning, always bathes in sacred fords / is freed from all sins and attains the supreme Brahman. / Bathing is declared to be fourfold by the wise who know bathing: / it is remembered as Vāyavya (airy), Vāruṇa (watery), Divya (celestial), and Brāhma (spiritual). / Vāyavya is bathing in the dust of cows; Vāruṇa is [bathing] in the ocean and the like; / Brāhma is enjoined by brahmin mantras; Divya is the water of the clouds in sunshine. / And among all bathings, the Vāruṇa bath there is superior. / A brahmin, a kṣatriya, and a vaiśya should perform the bath with mantras. / For a śūdra, however, it is remembered as done silently, and likewise for women. / A girl, a young woman, an old woman, men, women, and eunuchs— / are freed from all sins through the bath in Kārtika and Māgha. / Having bathed in Kārtika, people surely attain the desired fruit. / Formerly, at the auspicious Puṣkara, at the confluence of the Nandā, / Prabhañjana was freed at that very moment from his birth as a tiger. / Through the word of Nandā herself, she went to the highest [abode] in Kārtika. / Thus the rule for bathing has been declared. What more do you wish to hear?

2.4.m: Those who have performed the gift of a lamp according to rule in the month of Kārtika

He who reverently gives oil for a lamp to one engaged in the study of the Veda—

One should offer various kinds of lamps in the presence of Viṣṇu in Kārtika.

Wherever that goddess born of the ocean sees lamps,

2.4.m: Therefore, a lamp should always be placed during the month of Kārtika.
The gift of a lamp is especially prescribed for those who desire wealth and beauty:
particularly in a temple, on a riverbank, or on the king's highway.
He who gives a lamp in a place of sleep has fortune facing him on every side.

2.4.m: Seeing the house of a feeble person devoid of a lamp, he who provides one,
whether [that person be] a brahmin or of another caste, is exalted in Viṣṇu's world.

2.4.m: he who offers gifts of lamps does not go to hell.
He who properly gives a lamp at Pañcanada during the night—
in his lineage are born sons who are the illuminators of their family.
[Whatever fruit is gained] by the gift of food during the fortnight of the ancestors, and by water in the months of Jyeṣṭha and Āṣāḍha,
the fruit of that belongs in Kārtika to those who rekindle another's lamp.
By rekindling another's lamp and by serving the devotees of Viṣṇu,
one obtains in Kārtika the fruit of the royal consecration and the horse sacrifice.
Formerly, a twice-born named Harikara, who was constantly devoted to sin,
made an offering of a lamp in Kārtika in the course of gambling.
By the power of that merit, that best of the twice-born attained heaven.
Formerly, by the gift of a sky-lamp, Dharmanandana,
that king, mounted an excellent aerial chariot and went to Viṣṇu's world.
Whoever places a camphor lamp in front of Viṣṇu in Kārtika,

and having repeatedly said, 'Victory! Victory!', became a lord of kings. (34)

Nārada said:

2.4.s: bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptirhi nāsti me kamalāsana ..
