2.4.m: Speak further, O lotus-seated one, for I have no satiety;
by drinking the nectar of your speech, my thirst increases all the more. (1)
Brahmā said:
Having bathed at dawn and become purified, devoted to Viṣṇu in the month of Kārtika,
worshiping the god Dāmodara with tender tulasī leaves,

2.4.s: sa tu mokṣamavāpnoti nā'tra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 2 ..
2.4.d: स तु मोक्षमवाप्नोति नाऽत्र कार्या विचारणा .. 2 ..
2.4.m: he attains liberation; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. (2)
However, whoever, devoid of devotion, worships with gold and other riches—

2.4.s: tasya pūjāṃ na gṛhṇāti nā'tra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 3 ..
2.4.d: तस्य पूजां न गृह्णाति नाऽत्र कार्या विचारणा .. 3 ..
2.4.m: He does not accept his worship; no doubt should be entertained in this matter. (3)
For all classes alike, this devotion is considered supreme;

2.4.s: bhaktyā virahitaṃ karma na viṣṇoḥ priyakāraṇam .. 4 ..
2.4.d: भक्त्या विरहितं कर्म न विष्णोः प्रियकारणम् .. 4 ..
2.4.m: an act devoid of devotion does not bring pleasure to Viṣṇu. (4)
Continually worshiped with devotion with even half a leaf of tulasī,
the blessed Lord Hari personally becomes visible. (5)
In ancient times Viṣṇudāsa, through devotion and the worship of tulasī,
went swiftly to the world of Viṣṇu, while the Cola king obtained secondary rank. (6)
Hear the māhātmya of tulasī, which destroys sin and increases merit,
which was spoken by Viṣṇu of old to Ramā; that I now declare. (7)

2.4.s: saṃprāpte kārtike māsi tulasyāḥ pūjanaṃ hareḥ..
2.4.d: संप्राप्ते कार्तिके मासि तुलस्याः पूजनं हरेः..
2.4.m: When the month of Kārtika arrives, worship of Hari with tulasī—

2.4.s: ye kurvaṃti narā bhaktyā te yāṃti paramaṃ padam ..8..
2.4.d: ये कुर्वंति नरा भक्त्या ते यांति परमं पदम् ..8..
2.4.m: the men who perform it with devotion go to the supreme abode. (8)
Therefore, by every effort, with tender leaves of tulasī,
the destroyer of all afflictions is to be worshiped with great devotion. (9)
As far as a planted tulasī extends its roots,
for that many thousands of yugas one is glorified in the world of Brahmā. (10)
If one takes a bath in water combined with tulasī leaves,
he is freed from all sins and rejoices in the abode of Viṣṇu. (11)
And if one prepares a grove for planting [tulasī], O great sage,
by that alone his sins are cleared away and he is fit for absorption into brahman. (12)
In whose house, O brahmin, a tulasī grove stands,

2.4.s: tadgṛhaṃ tīrthabhūtaṃ tu na yāṃti yamakiṃkarāḥ .. 13 ..
2.4.d: तद्गृहं तीर्थभूतं तु न यांति यमकिंकराः .. 13 ..
2.4.m: that house becomes a sacred ford; the attendants of Yama do not go there. (13)
The tulasī grove removes all sins, yields merit, and grants desires;

2.4.s: ropayaṃti narāḥ śreṣṭhāste na paśyaṃti bhāskarim .. 14 ..
2.4.d: रोपयंति नराः श्रेष्ठास्ते न पश्यंति भास्करिम् .. 14 ..
2.4.m: the excellent men who plant it never see the son of the Sun. (14)
The person who wears sandal-paste mixed with tulasī wood,

2.4.s: taddehaṃ na spṛśetpāpaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ tathaiva ca .. .. 15 ..
2.4.d: तद्देहं न स्पृशेत्पापं क्रियमाणं तथैव च .. .. 15 ..
2.4.m: sin being committed does not touch his body in that way. (15)
Where the shadow of a tulasī grove falls, O twice-born,
a śrāddha should be performed there for the satisfaction of the ancestors. (16)
On whom a tulasī leaf is seen upon the ear or on the head,

2.4.s: yamastaṃ nekṣituṃ śaktaḥ kimu dūtā bhayaṃkarāḥ .. 17 ..
2.4.d: यमस्तं नेक्षितुं शक्तः किमु दूता भयंकराः .. 17 ..
2.4.m: Yama is not able to look at him, how much less his terrifying messengers? (17)
Whoever, full of reverence, listens daily to the greatness of tulasī,
his soul freed from all sin, goes to the world of Brahmā. (18)
In this very context they cite this ancient legend
concerning tulasī, O brahmin, which destroys sin through hearing. (19)
Formerly, in the land of Kaśmīra, there were two brahmins,
named Harimedhas and Sumedhas, wholly devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu, (20)
endowed with compassion for all living beings, and knowers of the meaning of all truth.
Once, those two best of twice-born men, intent on pilgrimage to sacred fords, (21)
were traveling together, overpowered with fatigue in a wilderness;
there those two subduers of foes saw a grove of tulasī. (22)
Seeing that great grove of tulasī, Sumedhas among them,
having then circumambulated it, bowed down full of devotion. (23)
Seeing this, Harimedhas, with the highest joy,

2.4.s: jñātuṃ tulasyā māhātmyaṃ tatphalaṃ ca punaḥpunaḥ .. 24 .. ..
2.4.d: ज्ञातुं तुलस्या माहात्म्यं तत्फलं च पुनःपुनः .. 24 .. ..
2.4.m: in order to learn the māhātmya of tulasī and its fruit again and again, said: (24)
Harimedhas said:

2.4.s: kimarthaṃ vipra deveṣu tīrtheṣu ca vrateṣu ca ..
2.4.d: किमर्थं विप्र देवेषु तीर्थेषु च व्रतेषु च ..
2.4.m: For what reason, O brahmin, when gods, sacred fords, and vows,
and foremost brahmins are present, have you offered obeisance [here]? (25)
Sumedhas said:
Listen, fortunate brahmin; you have spoken well.
The heat indeed oppresses both of us. Having gone to the presence of this banyan tree,
and resorting to its shade, I will tell you according to the truth.
Having spoken thus, Sumedhas, accompanied by Harimedhas,
who knew righteousness, went to the banyan tree endowed with a large hollow.
Resting there, that brahmin spoke indeed to Harimedhas:
“Let the excellent story of Tulasī be heard, O tiger among brahmins,
who arose in the ocean of milk through the grace of the Supreme Lord.
Formerly, when Puraṃdara’s sovereignty was lost through the curse of Durvāsas,
Brahmā and others, along with the gods and asuras, churned the ocean of milk.
Airāvata, the wish-fulfilling tree, the Moon, and Kamalā;
Uccaiḥśravas, the Kaustubha gem, and likewise Dhanvantari and Hari;
and the myrobalan and other divine medicinal plants—
these were born, O best among the twice-born, bestowing welfare upon the world.
Then, holding in both hands the pot of nectar
that grants agelessness and immortality—the supreme, beautiful vessel—

2.4.s: avekṣya manasā sadyaḥ parāṃ nirvṛtimāpa ha .. 33 ..

2.4.m: Viṣṇu, seeing it with his mind, immediately attained supreme bliss.
Tears of joy fell into that pot of nectar,
and instantly Tulasī was born, circular in form,
endowed with all auspicious marks, adorned with all ornaments.

2.4.s: tatrotpannāṃ tathā lakṣmīṃ tulasīṃ ca dadurhareḥ ..

2.4.m: The gods, Brahmā and the rest, then gave Lakṣmī, who had arisen there, and Tulasī to Hari;
and the blessed Lord Hari accepted [them].
Thenceforth, Tulasī became exceedingly dear to the Lord of the worlds.
She, the beloved, is worshipped like Viṣṇu by all the hosts of gods.
Nārāyaṇa is the protector of the universe, and Tulasī is his beloved.
Therefore obeisance was made to her by me, O brahmin.”
As the high-souled Sumedhas was speaking thus,
a great aerial chariot, radiant like the sun, was seen nearby.
At that moment, O sage, the banyan tree fell before [them].
And likewise from that tree two men emerged,
illuminating all quarters with their splendour, resembling the sun.
The two of them bowed down to Harimedhas and Sumedhas.
Harimedhas and Sumedhas, seeing them, were overcome with fear.
Filled with wonder, the two said to those two who resembled gods:
Harimedhas and Sumedhas said:
“Who are you two, who resemble gods and are all-auspicious,
wearing garlands of fresh mandāra flowers, like immortals,
worthy of our salutation and worship, having the form of celestials?”
Thus addressed by the two brahmins, the two who had emerged from the tree said:

2.4.m: “You two alone are our father, mother, and likewise teacher;

Surrounded by a group of apsarases, once to the Nandana forest

The celestial women dallied with me as they pleased.
Garlands of jasmine and pearls fell from those women
upon Romaśa while he was practising austerity. Seeing that, the sage was angered.
‘This is not the fault of the women, who are indeed dependent upon others;
this wicked-mannered one alone deserves a curse,’ he said.

‘When you hear from a twice-born the māhātmya of the tulasī leaf

2.4.s: yadā śṛṇoṣi sadyastvaṃ vimuktiṃ yāsyase parām..
2.4.d: यदा शृणोषि सद्यस्त्वं विमुक्तिं यास्यसे पराम्..

Formerly, this best of sages was devoted to serving his guru.
Having disregarded the command of his guru, he attained the state of a brahmarākṣasa.”

2.4.m: Having said this and bowed repeatedly to those two excellent sages,

Therefore, O Nārada, in this month of Kārtika which delights Hari,

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Tulasī', in the Kārtikamāsamāhātmya in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa in eighty-one thousand verses.
The Vālakhilyas said:
Kṛṣṇa spoke to Dharma concerning the twelfth [lunar day] named Vatsā:
The twelfth tithi joined with the twilight hour of cow-dust is [prescribed] for the worship of the calf. 1.
The worship of the calf is indeed to be performed at a banyan tree on the first day.
Having smeared with sandalwood and the like a cow with her calf, of uniform colour,
well-behaved and yielding milk, one should worship her with flower garlands. 2.
On that day, O Yudhiṣṭhira, food cooked in oil and cooked in a pot,
cow's milk and cow's ghee, as well as curds and milk, one should avoid. 3.
At the close of the day, half a ghaṭī on both sides of half the sun's orb,
the waving of lamps should then be performed, and one should observe the auspicious and the inauspicious. 4.
Having first arranged various lamps placed in golden vessels and the like,
one should wave the lamps beforehand and observe the auspicious and the inauspicious. 5.
Having lighted all the lamps, one should place them facing the north;

nine principal lamps are declared, and one may prepare others as well. 6.
If the flame rests toward the south, luminous and possessed of a crest,
and if steady, it is said to bestow happiness; but the opposite bestows sorrow. 7.
In the dark fortnight of Kārtika, on the five tithis beginning with the twelfth,
the rite of waving lamps in the first part of the night is declared for men. 8.
The first lamp indicates a fortnight, and the second a month;
the third indicates a season here, and the fourth a solstice likewise;
while the fifth lamp determines the auspicious and inauspicious for the year. 9.
'Born of a portion of the sun, destroyers of darkness,
may the lamps illuminate me at the three junctures of time and indicate the auspicious and inauspicious.' 2.4.9.10.
Having consecrated [them] with the mantra, one should then wave the lamps in order: 11.
First the deities, then the brahmins, elephants, and horses,
elders, superiors, inferiors, and women headed by mothers. 12.
Then one should place the waved lamps in their respective places;
by rough flames there would be destruction of wealth; by white ones, loss of food;

A cowherd woman named Ekāṅgī performed this observance;
endowed with wealth and grain, she became [prosperous] within three years. 14. / Therefore, the worship of cows is to be performed on the twelfth of Kārtika.
Those men who, having heard this māhātmya of the cow observance, perform it, 15.
by the power of the cow observance they are not separated from cattle on earth;
whatever offense against cows may have been committed dissolves through the observance. 16.
The Vālakhilyas said:
On the fourteenth lunar day in the dark fortnight, in the month of Āśvina,
near the festival of lamps, one should perform this observance. 17.
Having bathed in the morning on the thirteenth and cleaned one's teeth,
undertaking a rule of three nights, intent on devotion to Govinda, 18.
at the end of this observance, the Govardhana festival is likewise to be performed.
An overlap of more than three muhūrtas is to be accepted; an overlapping with the next day incurs no fault. 19.
In the dark fortnight of Āśvina, on the thirteenth at nightfall,
one should offer the lamp and an oblation to Yama; untimely death is destroyed. 2.4.9.20.

2.4.m:
Anciently, the young boy of Hemanaka was freed from untimely death
on the dark thirteenth of Āśvina through compassion. 21.
The messengers said:
"Tell [us] the means, O Yama, having shown mercy before us,
so that one may not fall from life during such a great festival!"
Yama said:
"In the dark fortnight of Āśvina, on the thirteenth day, at nightfall,
whoever offers a fine lamp at the door of his house every year,
with this mantra, O messengers, must not be brought by you during the festival;
even if premature death has arrived, my command must be obeyed:
'Together with Death, with the noose and the staff, and with Time and me,
may the son of the Sun be pleased by the offering of a lamp on the thirteenth day!'
Whoever presents a lamp at the doorway with this mantra
has no fear during the festival, nor of premature death."
The Vālakhilyas said:
"On the fourteenth day overlapped by the preceding tithi, in the other-than-bright [i.e., dark]
fortnight of Āśvina, one should diligently perform a ritual ablution at daybreak.

2.4.m:
A person who bathes on this empty day at a time other than dawn,
his religious merit accumulated over a year is surely destroyed; there is no doubt.
Likewise, on the dark fourteenth in Āśvina, at sunrise, O gods,
an oil massage is distinguished in the last watch of the night.
If the fourteenth day does not occur on two days at moonrise,
or even if it occurs on both days, then the earlier one alone is taken.
If out of obstinacy, stubbornness, or even supposed refinement, one does not perform
the oil massage on the fourteenth, he goes to the Raurava hell.
Lakṣmī resides in the oil, and the Gaṅgā in the water on the fourteenth of Dīpāvalī;
whoever performs the morning bath indeed does not see the world of Yama.
Then apāmārga, and tumbī, and prapunnāḍa as well—
one should wave them during the bath indeed for the destruction of hell,
three times, having recited the excellent mantra three times:
'O apāmārga, endowed with clods of the furrow, furnished with thorny leaves,
remove sin, being waved again and again!'

Here itself, the rule of bathing for one desirous of prosperity is told by me:
On the fourteenth and on the new moon of Iṣa, and on the first day of Kārtika,
when one bathes, one should take an oil bath at moonrise;
and on the tithi of the bright second of Ūrja, when the moon is in Svātī,
a person who takes an auspicious bath is never separated from Lakṣmī.
Because of the waving of lights with lamps here, this is called Dīpāvali.
Even on the new moon, an equinox, a Sunday, during a vyatīpāta, or on a dinakṣaya,
an oil massage in the morning here does not incur fault, for the sake of dispelling sins.
Having eaten the greens of māṣa leaves on that day,
on the fourteenth named Preta, a person is liberated from all sins.
On the dark fourteenth of Iṣa, and on the tithi of the new moon,
at the start of the new moon combined with Svātī, then Dīpāvali should take place.
One should observe this continuous three-day festival of lamps.

Having heard this speech of Viṣṇu, Bali spoke [these] words:
'What is to be asked for myself? Everything has already been given by me.'
"I shall ask for the sake of the world; if you are able, grant that to me.
Today the earth was given by me to you, who assumed the disguise of the Dwarf (Vāmana).
And since it was traversed by you in three steps during three days,
therefore let there be sovereignty on the surface of the earth for three days, O Hari.
Whatever mortals make gifts of lamps on earth during my reign,
may this wife of yours [Lakṣmī] remain forever firmly established in their house.
In whosever home darkness shall fall during my reign,
let the darkness [of the loss] of Lakṣmī and offspring forever fall upon their home.
And those who offer lamps on the fourteenth [day] for [the prevention of] Naraka,
all their ancestral multitudes shall not dwell in Naraka.
Those by whom rows of lamps (dīpāvali) are not made when Bali's reign arrives—
how shall lamps blaze in their home, O Keśava?
Those people who cause sorrow and lack of joy during Bali's reign,

One should ask, "Let there be Bali's reign during the three [days beginning with] the fourteenth."
Formerly, having begged for this earth in the form of a dwarf,
[Hari] gave [it] to Indra the son of Aditi, and [sent] Bali to dwell in Pātāla.
Thus those three days were granted by Hari to the lord of the Daityas;
therefore, indeed, one should arrange a great festival at this time by every means.
O best of sages, the Great Night (Mahārātri) arose on the fourteenth;
therefore its festival must be celebrated by those intent on the worship of Śakti.
When Bali's reign arrives, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras,
herbs, Piśācas, mantras, and jewels—
all become gladdened and dance at dusk.
And those various mantras attain perfection during Bali's reign; of this there is no doubt.
Just as people are extremely delighted when Bali's reign arrives,
so during those days people should be exceedingly joyful.

In the month of Āśvina, the three lunar days beginning with the fourteenth (bhūta) are proclaimed;
for deeds such as giving lamps, those prevailing at midday are to be accepted.
If these three lunar days occur prior to the saṃgava period,

having bathed and worshipped the gods and ancestors with devotion, and having bowed down,
and having performed the pārvaṇa-śrāddha with curd, milk, clarified butter, and so forth,
one should not eat by day on that occasion, except for children and the sick.
Then at the hour of dusk, one should worship auspicious Indirā [Lakṣmī].
One should make a spotless pavilion for Lakṣmī with various kinds of cloths,
and decorated with various flowers, tender sprouts, and paintings.
There one should worship Lakṣmī and also worship the gods.
The divine women too should be worshipped with many offerings,
and one should massage the feet of Lakṣmī and the others with devotion.
On this day in ancient times, all the gods were released by Viṣṇu
from the prison of Bali, and Lakṣmī too was liberated.
Then, together with Lakṣmī, the gods returned to the ocean of milk;
they slept happily for a long time. Therefore, O best of sages,
couches with cord netting and good mattresses should be prepared,
covered with cloths resembling milk foam in the respective directions.

2.4.m:
One should install those gods and Lakṣmī, accompanied by the chanting of the Vedas.
Lakṣmī, freed from the fear of the Daityas, slept comfortably within the belly of a lotus.
Therefore, here the ceremony of happy sleep should be performed according to rule for her satisfaction.
He who on that day [makes] a lotus-bed for the increase of the happiness of Padmā,
having left his house, that Padmā would never go anywhere else.
Those men who do not thus perform the happy sleep of Lakṣmī,
how indeed do they, devoid of anxiety for wealth, sleep at night?
Therefore, with every effort, a man should worship Lakṣmī;
freed from poverty, he will be established within his own class.
Having boiled cow’s milk combined with mace, cloves, cardamom,
cinnamon, and camphor, having added sugar as appropriate,
he should make laddus from it and offer them to Lakṣmī.
He should present other fourfold foods, saying: 'May Śrī be pleased.'
Before Hari has awakened, one should first have women awaken Lakṣmī.

2.4.m:
Whatever woman—or man—awakens Lakṣmī at the time of awakening and eats,
for an entire year Lakṣmī does not abandon them.
Having received freedom from fear from the brahmins, the enemies of the gods, terrified of Viṣṇu,
praised Śrī in the Ocean of Milk, knowing that she was asleep, reposing in a lotus:
"You are light, Śrī, the sun, moon, fire, lightning, gold, and stars;
the light of all lights, stationed in the light of lamps, reverence to you!
The Lakṣmī who, on the sacred day of Dīpāvalī upon the earth,
and in the cowshed of cattle on Kārttikā [is present], may that Lakṣmī be a granter of boons to me!"
Then at dusk he should make a gift of lamps and likewise wave a firebrand
around his own head, which wards off all misfortunes.
Likewise, lamp-trees should be set up according to one’s means in temples of the deities and elsewhere,
at crossroads, in cremation grounds, at rivers, mountains, and dwellings,
at the roots of trees, in cow-pens, in courtyards, and in houses.
The grounds of the royal highway should be adorned with cloths and flowers.
Having adorned the entire city, then at dusk,

having first fed the brahmins, and having fed the hungry,
adorned and shining in fresh garments, one should dine.
Then, in the afternoon, the king should proclaim to the city:
"Today is the reign of Bali; people, play as you wish!"
Having thus ordered, "Let children play as they wish!" the king
should give playthings to them, and then observe the good and bad.
Whatever is in one's mind should be done during Bali's reign—
[except that] injury to living beings, drinking liquor, intercourse with forbidden women,
theft, and breach of trust: these five, O best of sages,
are declared to be gates to hell during the reign of Bali, and must be abandoned.
Then at midnight the king himself should go into the city
on foot, very slowly, to view the delightful [sight],
and having seen the joy of Bali's reign, he should return to his house.
When midnight has passed in this manner and people's eyes are half-shut in sleep,
then by the women of the city, beating winnowing baskets and small drums,

2.4.m:
Alakṣmī is driven out from the courtyards of their houses by those [women] who are joyful.
If the conjunction of a single daṇḍa of night and the new moon occurs on the next day,
then leaving the previous day, the night of happiness is on the next day.
Those men, Vaiṣṇavas and non-Vaiṣṇavas, who do not celebrate the festival of Bali's reign,
their religious duties are in vain; of this there is no doubt.
At night one should keep vigil by reading the Purāṇas and the like,
or by playing dice in front of Hari, or likewise with singing.
Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled 'Description of the Duties on Vatsadvādaśī, Yamatrayodaśī, Narakacaturdaśī, and Dīpāvalī,' in the Māhātmya of the Month of Kārttika, in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

2.4.m:
2.4.9.14
On this matter there is a well-known story in the Sanatkumārasaṃhitā:
In ancient times there was an Ābhīra named Hṛṣīkeśa, a keeper of eight thousand cows. A daughter named Ekāṅgī was born to him. In the absence of a son, he performed extensive charitable deeds and religious acts for the sake of obtaining a son, and by means of that a son was born. Then his priest, named Dundubhi, who was one-eyed and greedy, came there and, out of avarice, untruthfully said: "He was born under the Mūla asterism." Then the frightened father said to his daughter: "O Ekāṅgī, 'Quickly take this boy, put ghee and honey in his mouth, / and swiftly cast him into the Gaṅgā for the increase of our happiness.'" Then Ekāṅgī, taking him out of compassion, placed him in the hollow of a great tree. "Coming repeatedly by day and by night, / nursing him with milk, she would return again to her own home. / In merely a year, that boy was able to speak sweet words, / and Ekāṅgī too became a maiden whose body was possessed by youth." One day the priest Dundubhi propositioned Ekāṅgī with lustful intent. Then she rebuked him. Out of hatred because of that, Dundubhi said to her father: "O Hṛṣīkeśa, I saw this daughter of yours sporting with Yavanas. A boy was born from a Yavana and he has been placed in the hollow of a tree. Go and look! Alas, your lineage is ruined; casting her out is indeed proper, otherwise there will be excommunication." Having heard this, Hṛṣīkeśa, in the manner told by the priest, bound Ekāṅgī and her [foster-]son to the back of a bull and abandoned them in the forest. By destiny that bull, taking her, went to Haridvāra, and the bondage became loosened. Then Ekāṅgī built a hut there, sold grass, and with that money maintained the boy and the bull. When the month of Kārtika arrived, people came from various countries for ritual ablution. Knowing her to be a cowherdess, they gave her cows brought for donation to protect. She also undertook great service to the cows. Then, together with the Vaiṣṇavas, she performed cow-worship on the twelfth day. Thus she did for three years. There, by destiny, Hṛṣīkeśa came together with the priest Dundubhi. Seeing his own daughter there, being utterly astonished, and having learned the true events from her, he arranged her marriage. And Dundubhi was condemned, and she too uttered a curse: "From this day forth, may those who place trust in a one-eyed man certainly go to destruction!" Having thus cursed him, giving the boy to her father and instructing [him] in the cow-vow, she departed herself with her husband. .. 14 ..

kāryārambhaḥ ekāṃgīdṛṣṭyā eva bhavati. kālakrameṇa yadāyadā anubhave vṛddhiḥ bhavati, tadaiva sarvāṅgīṇa dṛṣṭiḥ upalabhyate. dundubhipurohitaḥ api ekāṃgī dūradṛṣṭiḥ asti yaḥ kāṇī asti.

कार्यारम्भः एकांगीदृष्ट्या एव भवति. कालक्रमेण यदायदा अनुभवे वृद्धिः भवति, तदैव सर्वाङ्गीण दृष्टिः उपलभ्यते. दुन्दुभिपुरोहितः अपि एकांगी दूरदृष्टिः अस्ति यः काणी अस्ति.

2.4.m:
The commencement of an action happens from a one-sided perspective alone. Gradually over time, whenever there is an increase in experience, only then is a comprehensive vision attained. The priest Dundubhi too is an illustration of a one-sided, defective vision, being one-eyed.
The māhātmya and the procedure of the Govatsadvādaśī vow of the bright fortnight of Kārtika are also found in Bhaviṣyapurāṇa 4.69. Note on Vatsa.

2.4.m:
2.4.9.42
The offering of water to Yama has already been stated, and he will describe the offering of water to Bhīṣma later in the vow of Bhīṣmapañcaka. A lamp should be offered to Naraka, to the demon Naraka. On this point, there is an elaboration in the Sāroddhāra:
"Formerly, in the Saurīva country, there was a courtesan dear to people, / named Līlāvatī, virtuous and devoted to devotion to Hari. / Once, she joyfully approached the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha; / endowed with modesty, she inquired about the māhātmya of the fourteenth day. / Vasiṣṭha said: / 'Having performed the vow in this manner on the thirteenth, at moonrise in the night, / a bath with sesame oil should be taken by men who fear hell. / And that lunar day is called Nārakī, renowned among the worlds. / Formerly, from Lord Varāha, one named Naraka was born / upon the earth; and that wicked soul conquered all the gods, / and that evil-minded one stole the sovereignty of the gods. / At that time, all the deities went to Kṛṣṇa for refuge, / and petitioned by them for the slaughter of Naraka, / Śrī Kṛṣṇa went to where the wicked-souled Naraka, son of the Earth, was. / Having slain Naraka along with his ministers on the fourteenth day of Kārtika, / the supreme Kṛṣṇa then granted a boon to the fourteenth day: / "Those who will perform oil-massage and donation of clothes and the like, / to them I give fame, renown, sons, and sovereignty." / Having thus granted boons to it, it became renowned on earth from that time on. / Because on that day Mahālakṣmī is present in the oil, / and Gaṅgā, sprung from the lotus foot of Viṣṇu, remover of the world's impurities, / indeed establishes her presence in that warm water. / If the fourteenth day should occur at the moonrise of the thirteenth / in the dark [fortnight] of Āśvina, it is called Nārakī. / Even during Vyatīpāta, Vaidhṛti, or on the day of [the death of] mother and father, / if it is Nārakī Caturdaśī, a bath must be taken with sesame oil. / A bath with sesame oil should be taken by women as well as by men, / by ascetics, widows, or the desireless, according to rule; / an oil-massage should be performed then, otherwise one would go to hell.'" .. 42 ..

2.4.m:
2.4.9.101
Here the specific detail in the Brāhmapurāṇa is: "Nārada said: 'By what means women may become beautiful, fortunate, endowed with good offspring, and devoted to their husbands—tell me that observance, O Lord Brahmā.' / Śrī Brahmā said: 'Listen, O best of brahmins, to the auspicious observance called Sukharātri, a secret granting peace and happiness, which I have not told to anyone. / In the month of Kārttika, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, is this excellent observance, by the mere performance of which women increase their good fortune. / Viṣṇu, the source of the universe, sleeps happily along with Lakṣmī on that night; therefore it is spoken of by people as the Janasuptikā. / On that night, having drawn with mineral pigments, in the Lord’s five colors, the Jīvarātri, that is Sukharātri, in one's own house, / one should then paint the forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others. And having obtained the permission of her husband for the sake of good fortune, / she should prepare the worship offerings for the rite. / Then, having diligently anointed the body with fragrant substances, / women should take a bath in pleasantly warm water, O best of the twice-born. / Having bathed, put on delightful garments according to rule, / and having caused the installation of Sukharātri to be performed by a brahmin, / the deities beginning with Sukharātri must be worshipped according to rite with perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice grains, and the like, by women accompanied by their friends: / 'The deity of the domestic dwelling who has been drawn by me as Sukharātri—may she accept the worship offered by me, and may she grant me happiness. / Salutations to you, O Sukharātri, giver of life, bestower of happiness, beloved of Śiva! Accept this worship indeed and protect the children. / Grant beauty, grant victory, grant knowledge, happiness, and wealth; give me wisdom, and grant all desires happily with esteem.' / Having thus prayed to that goddess amidst the sounds of songs and musical instruments, / the worship of Lakṣmī should then be performed with devotion by women together with their husbands, / with three offerings of worship and these mantras addressed to the beloved of Hari: / 'Hail, O Goddess, Mother of the universe, residing on Viṣṇu's chest! O Ramā, salutations to you; grant me immovable good fortune here! / May that charming goddess Mahālakṣmī, who remains awake amid the row of lamps on the auspicious earth and rests on Hari's chest, grant me boons!' / Having thus praised the goddess Mahālakṣmī, the giver of happiness, / women should play at dice with their husband on Dīpāvalī, with the desire for victory, dependent on the husband: so said the Supreme Spirit. / The devoted wife who performs the endearing observance named Sukharātri in this manner according to the rite, / she truly becomes here endowed with sons, filled with wealth and grain, and possesses a living husband." Thus. 101.
Brahmā said:
Then, having performed an oil-massage on the first lunar day, followed by the waving of lamps,
well-dressed, one should spend the day with noble stories, songs, and gifts. 1.
Formerly, Śaṃkara initiated a delightful game of dice,
truly on the first day in the bright fortnight of Kārttika. 2.
Listen also to the māhātmya of the day of Bali's reign, in truth:
a bath with sesame oil must be taken by both men and women. 3.

Commentary:
Now he states the rule for Yamadvitīyā: 'yadīti'.
To explain the purpose of the name 'Yamadvitīyā', it is said also of the others in the Padma [Purāṇa]:
'O Skanda, these lunar days, beginning with the second, are indeed renowned.
Occurring over four months, they bring happiness during the rainy season.
The first is in the month of Śrāvaṇa, and another in Bhādrapada;
the third is in the month of Āśvayuja, and the fourth is in Kārtika.
In the month of Śrāvaṇa it is called Kaluṣā ('the turbid'), and likewise in Bhādrapada, Amalā ('the stainless');
in Āśvina it is called Pretasaṃcārā ('the roving of the deceased spirits'), and in Kārtika it is considered Yāmyakā ('sacred to Yama').
Formerly, when the slaying of Vṛtra had taken place and Puraṃdara had regained his kingdom,
the horse sacrifice was proclaimed to wipe away the sin of killing a brahmin.
Through his wrath, the sin of killing a brahmin was struck down by Indra with his thunderbolt.
It was cast upon the earth in six portions: into trees, water, the surface of the ground,
into woman, into the slayer of an embryo, and into fire, having been distributed in due order.
Before the hearing of that sin, on the day of the second [tithi], O sinless one,
woman, trees, rivers, earth, fire, and the slayer of an embryo,
became impure; therefore it is remembered as Kaluṣā ('the turbid').

Hearing the duty explained by the seer to the hunter, the brahmin [mouse],

Then, bowing to Viśvāmitra and recounting his own tale,
permitted by the seer, he mounted an aerial chariot and went to heaven.
The son of Gādhi was amazed, and especially so was the hunter.
The hunter too, having performed the vow of Ūrja, went to Hari's abode.
Therefore, by every effort in Kārtika, before Keśava,
taking shelter in the shade of a dhātrī tree, one should listen to the narrative.
Even a mouse was freed from an evil birth by hearing the narration of Ūrja;
whoever listens to it or recites it attains liberation, without a doubt.
Taking shelter under the shade of a dhātrī tree, one should partake of a meal in the forest,
having first performed ritual ablution in water located in the forest.
Having performed the daily rites, one should then worship Mādhava;
sheltered beneath the shade of a dhātrī tree, endowed with devotion to Hari,
one should listen to the celestial narrative extolling the greatness of the month.
Then with devotion one should feed brahmins, best among knowers of the Veda;
then, O best of brahmins, one should eat oneself, remembering Hari.
When the vow is thus performed in Kārtika, beloved of Hari, O brahmin,
the sin that is destroyed, O son, listen attentively:
from food not offered to Hari, from looking at the sun while eating,
and likewise from the sin of hearing the words of a menstruating woman during a meal,
and whatever fault of improper touch occurs at the time of eating,
from eating prohibited food, and from food defilement while eating—
as well as from discarding pure [food] during an auspicious time, O lover of Hari,
all the sin incurred by these [actions] is certainly destroyed. (64)

I shall tell you all of that ancient event, together with its legend.
In ancient times, Śakra went to Mount Kailāsa to see Śiva,
surrounded by all the gods and attended by crowds of apsarases.
As soon as he reached Śiva's abode, he saw there
a man of terrible deeds, fearsome with a fanged face.

2.4.m: As the ocean was speaking thus, that child, the ocean's son,
seized Brahmā by the beard, shaking him again and again.
As he shook his beard, water flowed from [Brahmā's] eyes.
Somehow freeing his beard, Brahmā then said to the ocean:
Brahmā said:
"Because this water of mine was drawn out from my eyes by him,
therefore he shall be celebrated by the name Jalandhara.
Right now he shall become a youth, master of all weapons and missiles.
He will be invulnerable to all living beings except Rudra.
Where he arose, there alone he will meet his end."
Nārada said:

Nārada said:
The daityas who had previously been conquered by the gods and were living in Pātāla,
they too came to the circle of the earth, taking refuge in him without fear.
Once, seeing Rāhu with his head cut off, that king of daityas
asked Bhārgava there the reason for his head being severed.
He told of the churning of the ocean brought about by the gods,
and the taking away of the jewels, and the defeat of the daityas.
Hearing of the churning of his own father, his eyes red with rage,
he dispatched a messenger, Ghasmara, into the presence of Śakra.
The messenger went to heaven and entered the excellent Sudharmā assembly hall.
With an unbowed head, he spoke astonishing words to the lord of the gods:
Ghasmara said:
"Jalandhara is the son of the ocean, the lord of all daitya folk.
I am a messenger sent by him; hear what he says:
'Why was my father, the ocean, churned by you with a mountain?

2.4.m: “Listen, messenger, to why the ocean was churned by me in the past.
Mountains terrified out of fear of me were placed inside its belly,
and other Daityas, who were my enemies, were also protected by it long ago.
Therefore, whatever was produced from it was indeed taken away by me.
Likewise Śaṅkha, the son of the ocean, previously hated the gods;
having entered the belly of the ocean, he was slain by my younger brother.
Therefore go and tell him the entire reason for the churning.”
Nārada said:
Thus dismissed by Indra, the messenger then went to earth.
He then reported all of these words to the Daitya.
Hearing that, the Daitya, his lip trembling with rage,
marched to heaven with the Daitya army to fight.
Then, in the battle, a great destruction of gods and Dānavas took place.
There in the battle, Bhārgava revived the dead Daityas

Likewise, in that battle, Aṅgiras revived the gods
by repeatedly bringing divine herbs from Mount Droṇa.

Nārada said:
Hearing that, Jalandhara, his body agitated with rage,
set out immediately, surrounded by millions of Daityas. (1)
As he set forth, Śukra and Rāhu came into his line of sight,
and slipping swiftly, his crown then fell to the ground. (2)
Then, crowded with the Daitya army and hundreds of aerial chariots,
the filled sky shone like [the heavens] covered with clouds during the monsoon. (3)
Seeing his preparation then, the gods led by Śakra,
went unseen and informed the Bearer of the Trident: (4)
The gods said:
Lord, all-pervading one, how do you not know of this calamity that has befallen the gods?
Therefore, for the sake of our protection, slay the son of the ocean! (5)
Nārada said:
Hearing this speech of the gods, the Bull-bannered [Śiva] laughed,
and having summoned Mahāviṣṇu, he spoke these words: (6)

And you have even gone to his house, leaving your own Vaikuṇṭha! (7)

The Gaṇas equipped themselves for battle in extreme haste,
all headed by Nandin, the Elephant-faced one, and the General of the Armies, by Śiva's command. (14)
Frenzied for battle, the Gaṇas swiftly descended from Kailāsa.
Then a battle broke out in the valley grounds of Kailāsa (15)
between the Pramatha lords and the Daityas, dense with terrible weapons and missiles,
accompanied by the sounds of hosts of kettle-drums, mṛdaṅgas, and conches that delighted heroes. (16)
Echoing with the noise of elephants, horses, and chariots, the earth trembled.
Filled with javelins, iron clubs, volleys of arrows, maces, spears, and scythes, (17)
the sky shone as if completely covered by meteors.
With the slain chariots, elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers, the ground appeared (18)
as though strewn with fragments of mountain peaks struck down by the thunderbolt.
With the hosts of Daityas slain by the Pramathas, and the Gaṇas slain by the Daityas, (19)
the ground, thick with mud of fat, blood, and flesh, then became impassable.
Bhārgava revived the hosts of Daityas slain by the Pramathas, (20)
again and again there in the battle, by the power of the Mṛtasaṃjīvinī [spell].

2.4.m: Seeing that, all the Gaṇas, thrown into confusion and filled with fear,
reported all that deed of Śukra to the God of gods. (21)
Then from the mouth of Rudra arose an exceedingly terrifying female spirit (Kṛtyā),
with shanks like palm trees, a cavernous mouth, and breasts that crushed down trees. (22)
Reaching the battlefield, devouring the great asuras,
and holding Bhārgava in her vulva, she disappeared into the sky.
Seeing Bhārgava held captive, the gaṇas then,
their faces unwithering, struck down the daitya army with joy, furious in battle.
Then the army of the daityas broke, afflicted with fear of the gaṇas,
scattered like a mass of grass struck by the force of the wind.
Seeing the army broken through fear of the gaṇas, filled with wrath,
the two generals Niśumbha and Śumbha, and the valiant Kālanemi, advanced.
Those three of great strength checked the army of gaṇas,
releasing showers of arrows like clouds in the rainy season.
Then those floods of the daityas' arrows, like swarms of locusts,
blocked the sky and all the directions, making the army of gaṇas tremble.
The gaṇas, pierced by hundreds of arrows, raining down torrents of blood,
resembled kiṃśuka trees in spring; nothing at all could be discerned.
Fallen and being felled, pierced and severed, the gaṇas then
abandoned the field of battle and all turned their backs.
Then, seeing their own force broken, Śailādi, Lambodara, and Kārtikeya,
filled with haste, being wrathful, forcibly held back the foremost daityas.

Seeing those leaders of the gaṇas—Nandin, Ibhamukha, and Ṣaṇmukha—
the dānavas rushed forward in wrath for single combat.
Kālanemi rushed at Nandin, Śumbha at Lambodara,
and Niśumbha, clad in armor, swiftly rushed at Ṣaṇmukha.
Niśumbha pierced the heart of Kārtikeya's peacock

Then, as soon as the spear-bearer angrily grasped his spear,
Niśumbha swiftly struck him down with his own spear.
Nandīśvara pierced Kālanemi with multitudes of arrows,
and with seven arrows severed his horses, his banner, and with three his charioteer.
Kālanemi, greatly enraged, cut Nandin's bow;
flinging it aside, the mighty one struck him in the chest with a trident.
With his heart pierced by the trident, his horses slain, and his charioteer killed,
he hurled a mountain peak and brought down Śailādi as well.
Then Śumbha and Gaṇeśa, mounted on chariot and rat,
fought and pierced each other with flights of arrows.

2.4.m: Then Gaṇeśa pierced Śumbha in the heart with a winged shaft,
and with three arrows brought his charioteer down to the ground.
Then the enraged Śumbha pierced the lord of gaṇas with sixty arrows,
and the rat with three, and roared with the sound of a cloud.
The rat, its limbs pierced by arrows, staggered in severe pain,
and Lambodara fell and became a foot-soldier, O king.

2.4.m: Then Lambodara, striking Śumbha in the chest with his axe,

Both Kālanemi and Niśumbha with arrows simultaneously struck
Lambodara in fury, as if striking a great elephant with goads.
Seeing him afflicted, Vīrabhadra of great might
then rushed forward swiftly, accompanied by ten million bhūtas.
Kūṣmāṇḍas, bhairavas, vetālas, troops of yoginīs,
hosts of piśācas and yoginīs, and the gaṇas followed him.
Then, with shrieks of joy, deep lion-roars,
kettledrums, cymbals, and mṛdaṅgas, the earth trembled.
Then the bhūtas rushed forward, devouring the dānavas;
they leapt up, swooped down, and danced upon the field of battle.
Nandin and Kārtikeya, recovering and acting with haste,
struck down the daityas in battle with continuous flights of arrows.
Cut to pieces, pierced, with daityas slain, fallen, and devoured then,
that army was thrown into confusion, its faces crestfallen.
Seeing his army utterly destroyed then, the son of the ocean,
the mighty one, advanced against the gaṇas in his chariot with towering banners.
The clatter of elephants, horses, and chariots, the sounds of conches and kettledrums,
and the lion-roars of both armies arose then.
With the volleys of Jalandhara's arrows, as if with banks of fog,
the space between heaven and earth became completely blocked.
Having pierced Gaṇeśa with five arrows, Śailādi with nine,
and Vīrabhadra with twenty, he roared with the sound of a cloud.
Then Kārttikeya swiftly pierced the Daitya with a spear;
pierced by the spear, his mind somewhat agitated, [Jalandhara] fought on.
Then, his eyes filled with wrath, Jalandhara struck Kārttikeya
with his mace, and he fell to the surface of the earth.
In the same way he swiftly felled Nandin to the surface of the earth;
then the lord of the Gaṇas, enraged, struck the mace with his axe.
Vīrabhadra pierced the Dānava in the chest with three arrows,
and with seven he cut down his horses, standard, bow, and umbrella.
Then the lord of the Daityas, exceedingly enraged, raised a terrible spear,
felled Gaṇeśa, and then mounted another chariot.
Then, filled with fury, he rushed with speed against Vīrabhadra;
then the two, resplendent as the sun, fought with each other.
Vīrabhadra once again brought down his horses with arrows;
having his bow cut, the lord of the Daityas leaped down, armed with an iron club.

2.4.m: What does Viṣṇu, when properly worshipped, not bestow upon embodied beings?
By him the son of Uttānapāda was placed in the state of the pole-star of old.
Merely by remembering his name, embodied beings attain the good state.
Indeed, of old, when seized by a crocodile, the king of elephants, by remembering his name,
was freed, attained his presence, and became this one named Jaya.
Because Viṣṇu was worshipped by you, you will attain his presence
for many thousands of years, together with your two wives.
Then, when your merit is exhausted and you go down to the surface of the earth,
you will become a renowned king born in the solar dynasty,
by name Daśaratha, there again joined with two wives,
and also with this third one, who shared half of your merit.
There too Viṣṇu will come into your presence on the surface of the earth,
manifesting himself in the state of your son, accomplishing the task of the immortals.

2.4.m: Vijaya, having heard his curse, also cursed him in turn:

Jaya and Vijaya said:
'We are both your devotees, O God; how can we enter the wombs of a crocodile and an elephant?

The Blessed Lord said:
'The word of two devotees of mine will never become false;
Even by me, it can never be made otherwise.
Indeed, of old I appeared in a pillar at the word of Prahlāda;
Likewise, truly, by the speech of Ambarīṣa, I was born in a womb myself.
Therefore, having experienced these two curses made by yourselves,
May you attain my eternal abode.' Having spoken thus, Hari disappeared.

The glorious Kṛṣṇa said:
Hearing his speech, Pṛthu, his mind filled with wonder,
duly worshipped Nārada and then sent him off, O beloved. (1)
In ancient times, in the city of Avantī, there was a certain brahmin named Dhaneśvara,
fallen from brahminical duties, of sinful deeds, and very wicked-minded. (2)
Going from country to country for the sake of buying and selling,
once that Dhaneśvara came to the city of Māhiṣmatī. (3)
It was founded formerly by Mahiṣa, and therefore it is called Māhiṣmatī,
where the sin-destroying Narmadā shines, touching its ramparts. (4)
Seeing people there who observed the Kārtika vows, arrived from various countries,
he lived there for one month, engaged in trade. (5)
Constantly wandering on the bank of the Narmadā for the sake of commerce,
he saw brahmins engaged in ritual ablution, recitation of mantras, and worship of deities; (6)
some reciting the Purāṇa, some engrossed in listening,
intent on dancing, singing, instrumental music, and hearing of Viṣṇu; (7)
some engaged in the concluding rite, some intent on keeping night vigils,
devoted to worshipping brahmins and cows, and devoted to giving lamps. (8)
Filled with curiosity, Dhaneśvara watched here and there;
wandering there constantly, through seeing, touching, and speaking with (9)
Vaiṣṇavas, he received the hearing of Viṣṇu's name and the like.
Thus the brahmin stayed for a month on the bank of that Narmadā. (10)

2.4.d: आत्मनो वा परस्याऽपि यदि सेवां न कारयेत् .. .. 46 ..
2.4.m: if he does not cause service to be rendered either to himself or to another.

Thus indeed, even though not given, merit and sin accumulated by another always arrive.
In the Kali age, however, this rule does not apply; indeed, the agent alone experiences [the fruit of] merit and sin.

2.4.s: kalau tvayaṃ vai niyamo na kāryaḥ kartaiva bhoktā khalu puṇyapāpayoḥ .. .. 47 ..
2.4.d: कलौ त्वयं वै नियमो न कार्यः कर्तैव भोक्ता खलु पुण्यपापयोः .. .. 47 ..
2.4.m: In the Kali age there is no firm knowledge; in the Kali age good deeds are done with pride;

2.4.s: kalau jñānaṃ dṛḍhaṃ nāsti kalau garveṇa satkriyā ..
2.4.d: कलौ ज्ञानं दृढं नास्ति कलौ गर्वेण सत्क्रिया ..
2.4.m: in the Kali age spiritual practice accompanied by hypocrisy surely perishes—there is no doubt.

2.4.s: kalau dambhā'nvito yogo naśyatyeva na saṃśayaḥ ..48..
2.4.d: कलौ दम्भाऽन्वितो योगो नश्यत्येव न संशयः ..48..
2.4.m: Formerly, one intent on austerity, though hypocritical, and a chaste wife, by virtue of purity,
and one serving the month of Kārttika through observing the worship of his parents, attained the highest state.

2.4.s:
pitroḥ pūjādarśanena corjasevī paraṃ gataḥ .. 49 ..**
.. .. nārada uvāca .. ..
2.4.d:
पित्रोः पूजादर्शनेन चोर्जसेवी परं गतः .. 49 ..**
.. .. नारद उवाच .. ..
2.4.m: Nārada said:
O Lord, I wish to hear of the best vow among vows,
the injunction for the month-long fast, and its proper fruit.
Brahmā said:

2.4.s: sādhu nārada sarvaṃ te yatpṛṣṭaṃ prabruve'nagha ..
2.4.d: साधु नारद सर्वं ते यत्पृष्टं प्रब्रुवेऽनघ ..
2.4.m:
Well asked, O sinless Nārada! I shall tell you all that was inquired of.
O best among the intelligent, listen with devotion as I speak.

2.4.s: bhaktyā matimatāṃ śreṣṭha śṛṇuṣva gadato mama .. 51 ..
2.4.d: भक्त्या मतिमतां श्रेष्ठ शृणुष्व गदतो मम .. 51 ..
2.4.m: Just as Viṣṇu is among the gods, and the sun among luminous bodies,

2.4.s: surāṇāṃ ca yathā viṣṇustapatāṃ ca yathā raviḥ ..
2.4.d: सुराणां च यथा विष्णुस्तपतां च यथा रविः ..
2.4.m: just as Meru is among mountain peaks, and Garuḍa among birds,
so also the month-long fast is the best of all vows.
Whatever merit is found in all vows, and in all sacred fords,
and whatever arises from all gifts and from sacrifices with abundant priestly fees,
one does not obtain such merit as is gained from fasting for a month.
Therefore, having received the command of the guru, one should undertake the month-long fast.
After performing the Atikṛcchra, the Pārāka, and then the Cāndrāyaṇa penances,

2.4.s: atikṛcchraṃ ca pārākaṃ kṛtvā cāṃdrāyaṇaṃ tataḥ .. 55 ..
2.4.d: अतिकृच्छ्रं च पाराकं कृत्वा चांद्रायणं ततः .. 55 ..
2.4.m: one should undertake the month-long fast, knowing the strength or weakness of one's body.
A forest hermit, an ascetic, or a widow, O sage,

2.4.s: vānaprastho yatirvāpi nārī vā vidhavā mune .. 56 ..
2.4.d: वानप्रस्थो यतिर्वापि नारी वा विधवा मुने .. 56 ..
2.4.m: should undertake the month-long fast by the command of a guru or a brahmin.
Having fasted on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of Āśvina,
one should undertake this vow for thirty days.
In a temple of Acyuta, one should worship Hari with devotion at the three junctures of the day,
with food offerings, incense, lamps, and the like, and with various kinds of flowers.
One should worship the one whose emblem is Garuḍa in mind, deed, and speech.
A man devoted to his own duty, a married woman who has subdued her senses,
or a virtuous widow should properly worship Vāsudeva.

2.4.s: nārī vā vidhavā sādhvī vāsudevaṃ samarcayet .. 2.4.30.60 ..
2.4.d: नारी वा विधवा साध्वी वासुदेवं समर्चयेत् .. 2.4.30.60 ..
2.4.m: Looking at objects, enjoying scents, and the like are declared as tasting;
one should avoid staying in another's house and accepting morsels of food.
Anointing the limbs, anointing the head, betel, and unctions—
one observing the vow should avoid all these, and whatever else has been forbidden.
The observer of the vow must not touch anyone engaged in improper conduct, nor converse with such a one.
Dwelling in a shrine of God, a householder too may observe the vow.
A man, having observed the month-long fast according to the prescribed rule,
neither less nor more, thus completes the vow in thirty days.
Then, on the twelfth day, he should certainly worship the auspicious one whose emblem is Garuḍa.
Having fed excellent brahmins and presented gifts of clothes and the like,
he should give them priestly fees and, bowing down, ask for their forgiveness.
Having asked forgiveness of the brahmins, worshipped them, and sent them off,
having chosen thirteen brahmins at the conclusion of the month-long fast,
and fasting on the eleventh day, he should cause a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice to be performed.
Then, preceded by prostrations, he should feed the brahmins.
Having given betel, pairs of garments, food, clothing,
meditation bands, sacred threads, and beds complete with furnishings
to the foremost of brahmins, and having honoured them, he should send them away.
Thus the rule for the month-long fast has been duly proclaimed.
Hereafter I shall declare the rule for the ninth and following lunar days.
Listen, O Nārada, to that which was spoken to the seers by the Vālakhilyas.

2.4.s: ṛṣibhyo vālakhilyaiśca proktaṃ taṃ śṛṇu nārada .. 71 ..
2.4.d: ऋषिभ्यो वालखिल्यैश्च प्रोक्तं तं शृणु नारद .. 71 ..
2.4.m: Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Rule for the Month-Long Fast Following the Narration of the Attainment of the Fruits of Bestowed Merit and Sin," in the glorification of the month of Kārttika, in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

2.4.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye dattapuṇyapāpaphalaprāptivarṇanapūrvaka māsopavāsavratavidhikathanaṃnāma triṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 30 ..
2.4.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे कार्तिकमासमाहात्म्ये दत्तपुण्यपापफलप्राप्तिवर्णनपूर्वक मासोपवासव्रतविधिकथनंनाम त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 30 ..
2.4.m: Thus ends the chapter.

2.4.m: On the words "devoted to tapas" [the commentator notes]: Here is the well-known story from the Brāhma [Purāṇa]: In the Tretāyuga, there was a deceitful brahmin named Taponiṣṭha who endured the dualities of life. Once, as he was wandering for alms, a crane flying in the sky dropped feces into the middle of the food in his bowl. The crane was looked at by him, and then it fell from its path in the sky; with his gaze of wrath, that crane lost its life in an instant. Seeing that, he became wicked and proud of his own power. Once, as he was wandering for alms, he went to a dwelling of a certain devoted wife and said, "Give alms!" Seeing the ascetic, she, devoted to serving her husband and busy performing her daily duties, found no interval to give alms. Well-mannered and wishing what was pleasing to him, she fed her husband; with the end of her garment, she warded off small insects. That ascetic also stood motionless like a post out of wrath. Having fed him, seeing her own husband cleansed and reclining on the bed, she wiped his feet; massaging his feet, with a smiling face, she spoke agreeable, pleasing, beneficial, and affectionate words concerning their relationship. Then, when her own husband had fallen asleep, the chaste, virtuous woman took a vessel of food and went outside. Seeing the chaste woman who now wished to give alms, the ascetic, his eyes reddened with fury, made a roaring sound and would not take what was offered by her. Then that virtuous woman, her eyes cast down at her own feet, said to him: The devoted wife said: "I am not that lovely crane which was burned by you, O great ascetic! The desire of your mind shall not come to pass; take the food!" Brahmā said: Then, highly astonished, the brahmin dropped that alms-bowl, his hair bristling, and with joined palms spoke to the chaste woman: The ascetic said: "How, O mother, do you know of the crane falling today, struck down from the sky? Tell me the reason for that!" The devoted wife said: "O brahmin, this is not produced by mantras or the like, nor is it inborn in me; it is merely the general power of whoever has Acyuta in their heart. For those who perform rituals, Viṣṇu is in the sacred fire; for sons, Hari is the parents; for women, he indeed resides in their husbands; for students, in the preceptor. In the brahmin for all castes, Viṣṇu is declared by the wise; Hari is in statues for the small-minded, and in the heart for yogins. This Ancient Person is my visible deity—father, mother, preceptor, protector, kinsmen, friend, and son. Truly, O brahmin, all that exists, being composed of all things, is present for me on earth in my husband. Through service to him, I have this knowledge and both worlds. As a woman under her husband's control, I should not speak to another, O twice-born; you had no right even to speak this much at present. This has been spoken because of the context; therefore may Viṣṇu be pleased with me! If you now desire to hear of dharma, O ascetic, go to Vārāṇasī and ask a meat-seller, a hunter dwelling in a slaughterhouse; he will tell you of dharma." Having said just this, she went into the inner apartment. The ascetic too, having gone to Vārāṇasī, went to the hunter's house. Seeing that ascetic approaching, he ran towards him; coming forward, the hunter bowed humbly to that brahmin, then brought him to his own home, worshipped him according to the rules, and said: "You have now been sent to my house by that chaste woman." Brahmā said: Hearing his speech, the ascetic was extremely astonished and said: "How do you, the righteous hunter, know of the devoted wife?" The righteous hunter said: "This power of mine is not produced by mantras or the like, nor is it inborn; I bow to my parents, hence such power is mine. Incomparable, correct, threefold-temporal, and unfailing knowledge, as well as the secret of dharma, I know through service to my parents." Having said this, he spoke again to the ascetic who was desiring instruction: "The brahmin is the highest among the castes, praised by all castes; therefore, a twice-born is never to be instructed by the low-born. Hence, go, O brahmin, to the seer named Bindu; possessing knowledge and righteous conduct, he will impart knowledge to you." Hearing his words, bowing to him and taking leave, he went to the sacred ford of Pañcanada and addressed the lord among sages: The ascetic said: "O brahmin-seer, what was accumulated previously by me has been destroyed through wrath. Now tell me out of mercy that by which I may attain liberation." The seer Bindu said: "Kārtika is remembered as the foremost of all dharmas. Likewise, O ascetic, all sacred fords take away the sins of living beings; Prayāgarāja takes away the sins of all sacred fords when the sun is in Capricorn; and the sacred ford of Pañcanada takes away the sin of Prayāgarāja in Kārtika. Therefore, go to Pañcanada and observe the Kārtika vow." Having heard that, the ascetic went there, performed the vow according to the rules, and went to the world of Viṣṇu on an aerial chariot. .. 49 ..

2.4.s: taponiṣṭa tāpasasya ṭīkāyāṃ bindoḥṛṣeḥ ullekhamasti yaḥ paṃcanadatīrthe vratakaraṇasya parāmarśaṃ dadāti. upaniṣadeṣu oṃkārasya saṃdarbhe sārvatrikarūpeṇa bindu evaṃ nādasya ullekhāḥ santi. bindoḥ sthitiḥ arvāk asti, nādasya uttarā. anekānāṃ bindūnāṃ ullekhamasti, yathā mūlādhārasya binduḥ, cakṣuṣaḥ binduḥ, manasaḥ binduḥ. patisevā, pitṛsevādi kāryāṇi bindusthitiprāpaṇasya caraṇāḥ santi, ayaṃ pratīyate. yāvat pāpaḥ vidyamānaḥ asti, tāvat binduvat saṃghananaṃ saṃbhavaṃ nāsti. bindu avasthā prāptyuttaraṃ nādasya, nadasya prāptiḥ apekṣitā asti.
2.4.d: तपोनिष्ट तापसस्य टीकायां बिन्दोःऋषेः उल्लेखमस्ति यः पंचनदतीर्थे व्रतकरणस्य परामर्शं ददाति. उपनिषदेषु ओंकारस्य संदर्भे सार्वत्रिकरूपेण बिन्दु एवं नादस्य उल्लेखाः सन्ति. बिन्दोः स्थितिः अर्वाक् अस्ति, नादस्य उत्तरा. अनेकानां बिन्दूनां उल्लेखमस्ति, यथा मूलाधारस्य बिन्दुः, चक्षुषः बिन्दुः, मनसः बिन्दुः. पतिसेवा, पितृसेवादि कार्याणि बिन्दुस्थितिप्रापणस्य चरणाः सन्ति, अयं प्रतीयते. यावत् पापः विद्यमानः अस्ति, तावत् बिन्दुवत् संघननं संभवं नास्ति. बिन्दु अवस्था प्राप्त्युत्तरं नादस्य, नदस्य प्राप्तिः अपेक्षिता अस्ति.
2.4.m: [Modern commentary:] In the commentary on the ascetic Taponiṣṭha, there is mention of the seer Bindu, who advises the observance of the vow at the sacred ford of Pañcanada. In the Upaniṣads, in the context of the Praṇava (oṃkāra), there are ubiquitous mentions of bindu and nāda. The state of bindu is earlier, while that of nāda is later. There is mention of numerous bindus, such as the bindu of the mūlādhāra, the bindu of the eye, and the bindu of the mind. It appears that actions such as service to the husband and service to the parents are steps toward attaining the state of bindu. As long as sin exists, concentration like a bindu is not possible. After attaining the state of bindu, the attainment of nāda, of the flow (nada), is required.

Abandoning sinful thoughts, an intelligent man, observing celibacy,
must abandon liquor, meat, and sexual intercourse, which cause sin.
Subsisting on vegetables and the food of sages, a man devoted to the worship of Kṛṣṇa,
should then eat at night, preceded by [drinking] the five products of the cow.
In this way it should be properly completed, and he will obtain the stated reward.
Even a drunkard who drinks wine from birth until his death,
by observing this Bhīṣma vow, attains the supreme state.
It should also be observed by women with the consent of their husbands, to increase virtue,
and by widows, for the great enhancement of the bliss of liberation.
Formerly, in Ayodhyā, a king named Atithi,
having observed this very rare vow on the instruction of Vasiṣṭha,
enjoyed all pleasures here [on earth] and in the end went to the city of Viṣṇu.
Thus one should regularly perform the five-day observance called the Bhīṣmapañcaka,
with restriction, by fasting, or else with the five products of the cow,
subsisting on milk, roots, fruits, or sacrificial food, wholly intent upon the vow.

Note on Ekādaśī:
Īśvara said:
Listen, O best of the gods, to the māhātmya of Prabodhinī, which destroys sin and increases merit,
granting liberation to those whose intellect is fixed on truth.
The Gaṅgā, the Bhāgīrathī, roars on the earth only so long,
until Haribodhinī, which destroys sins, arrives in Kārtika.
The sacred fords and the lakes reaching as far as the ocean roar only so long,
until Prabodhinī, the lunar day of Viṣṇu, arrives in Kārtika.
[The fruit of] thousands of horse sacrifices and hundreds of Rājasūya sacrifices
is obtained by a single fast on Prabodhinī.
Whatever is rare and hard to obtain in the three worlds, with its moving and unmoving beings,
even that, when sought, O twice-born one, Pratibodhinī bestows.

Therefore, the awakening ceremony should be performed on the eleventh lunar day by Vaiṣṇavas:
“Arise, arise, Govinda! Arise, O Garuḍa-bannered Lord!
Arise, O beloved of Kamalā, and bring auspiciousness to the three worlds!”

Note on Ekādaśī
Nārada said:
For all vows, O Brahmā, a concluding ceremony has been heard of;
in the absence of a concluding ceremony, one never attains the fruit at any time.
In order to obtain the fruit of an observed vow, a wise person should perform the concluding ceremony;
otherwise, an observed vow, even if peerless, becomes completely fruitless.
Even the best vow among vows observed in Kārtika, O lord,
in the absence of its concluding ceremony, one would not attain the fruit declared for the vow.
Therefore, the ritual of concluding the month of Kārtika, O lord,
tell me, your best disciple, who have surrendered and am obedient to you.
Brahmā said:
Now I shall declare the concluding rite of Ūrja, which destroys all sins.
Listen to that with great devotion, together with its ritual, in brief.
On the bright fourteenth of Ūrja, the vow-keeper should perform the concluding ceremony,
in order to complete the vow and for the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu.
Over the tulasī plant he should erect an auspicious canopy.
[A pavilion] fitted with banana pillars, variegated with various minerals,
And in the four directions there a very beautiful row of lamps should be made,
With fine archways, four doorways, and adorned with flowers and chowries. // 8
At the doorways he should worship separately the clay gatekeepers:
Jaya and Vijaya, and Caṇḍa and Pracaṇḍa, // 9
Nanda and Sunanda, Kumuda and Kumudākṣa—
These he should worship at the four gates, endowed with devotion. // 10
At the base of the tulasī plant, [a diagram] called Sarvatobhadra
Should be well adorned and richly beautified with four colors. // 11
Above it, a water jar filled [with water] and endowed with jewels—
There he should worship the god bearing the conch, discus, and mace; // 12
He should worship him clad in yellow silk garments, accompanied by Lakṣmī.
And the observer of the vow should worship the world-guardians, beginning with Indra, in the pavilion. // 13
On that [night], he should fast with devotion, calm and with a mind bowed low;
At night, he should keep a vigil with the auspicious sounds of song, instruments, and the like. // 14

2.4.m: The māhātmya of the Kārttika full moon is embedded in Śiva's slaying of Tripura with a single arrow. The designation of the month of Āśvina is Iṣa. Iṣa—in [the sense of] wish, desire. Prior to engaging in an action or sacrifice, the awakening of desire regarding the action is necessary. Only then will the path of action be straight. Otherwise, just as the path of nature's growth is crooked, so it will be. It appears that the process of Iṣa, of creating desire, of fashioning a single arrow out of all arrows, is not completed in the month of Āśvina. For this reason, there is the injunction to produce a single arrow on the Kārttika full moon. In Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 25.1 there is a section called Iṣu, where the name of the Upasad offering is Iṣu. This mention is the transmission of the Purāṇic account into Vedic literature.

on the fourteenth, the gods along with sacrifices purify living beings;
on the full moon day, the auspicious sacred fords are situated by Viṣṇu. // 4
Whether killers of brahmins or drinkers of liquor, they purify all living beings.
Whoever bathes with warm water on the three days beginning with the Kārttika full moon, // 5
goes to the Raurava hell for as long as fourteen Indras [reign].
One incapable of the rule for the entire month should observe it during these three days; // 6
having obtained the full fruit by that, he rejoices in the abode of Viṣṇu.
That man who, directed toward the gods, the ancestors, Viṣṇu, or the teacher, // 7

2.4.s: na snānādi karotyaddhā sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam ..
2.4.d: न स्नानादि करोत्यद्धा स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् ..
2.4.m: does not perform ritual ablution and the like—he surely goes to hell.
A householder who feeds his family during those three days, // 8
having redeemed all his ancestors, goes to the supreme abode.

2.4.s: gītāpāṭhaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādaṃtime ca dinatraye .. 9 ..
2.4.d: गीतापाठं तु यः कुर्यादंतिमे च दिनत्रये .. 9 ..
2.4.m: And whoever recites the Gītā during the final three days, // 9
attains day after day the fruit of horse sacrifices, without a doubt.
Whoever recites the thousand names [of Viṣṇu] during the three days,
is never tainted by sins, like a lotus leaf by water.
Some men [have attained] divine status, and some have attained perfection itself.

2.4.s: tasya puṇyaphalaṃ vaktuṃ kaḥ śakto divi vā bhuvi ..
2.4.d: तस्य पुण्यफलं वक्तुं कः शक्तो दिवि वा भुवि ..
2.4.m: Who in heaven or on earth is able to describe the fruit of its merit?

2.4.s: yo vai bhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ śṛṇoti ca dinatrayam .. 12 ..
2.4.d: यो वै भागवतं शास्त्रं शृणोति च दिनत्रयम् .. 12 ..
2.4.m: He who listens to the scripture of the Bhāgavata for three days—
by some the state of Brahman was attained through devotion during the three days.
Liberation [is attained] through knowledge of Brahman, or through dying at Prayāga,
or else through observance during the three days in the month of Kārttika.

2.4.s: kārttike haripūjāṃ tu yaḥ karoti dinatraye .. 14 ..
2.4.d: कार्त्तिके हरिपूजां तु यः करोति दिनत्रये .. 14 ..
2.4.m: He who performs the worship of Hari during the three days in Kārttika
has no rebirth even after hundreds of millions of kalpas.
In the month of Kārttika, O best of brahmins, all [is auspicious] in the final three days;
even there, sinless one, special merit belongs to the full moon day.
Rising at dawn, one should perform purification, ritual ablution, and the like.
Having completed all rites, one should perform the worship of Viṣṇu.

2.4.s: udyāne vā gṛhe vā'pi kārttikyāṃ viṣṇutatparaḥ .. 17 ..
2.4.d: उद्याने वा गृहे वाऽपि कार्त्तिक्यां विष्णुतत्परः .. 17 ..
2.4.m: Either in a garden or at home on the Kārttika full moon, devoted to Viṣṇu,
one should construct a pavilion there, adorned with banana trunks,
covered with mango sprouts, and well adorned with sugarcane stalks.
Having decorated it with variegated cloths, one should worship the God there.
One should worship Hari with abundant mango sprouts, flowers, fruits, and the like.
A pure man, observing the vows, should listen to the Ūrjamāhātmya,
either completely, or a chapter, or even a single verse.
Or one should listen to the sacred story day by day for a muhūrta.
If a man is unable to listen every day,
he should listen during a sacred month or on a sacred lunar day.
By the power of that merit, a person becomes freed from sin.
A wise man, knowledgeable in the Purāṇas, pure, capable, calm, devoid of envy,

2.4.s: sādhuḥ kāruṇiko vāggmī vadetpuṇyāṃ kathāṃ sudhīḥ .. 23..
2.4.d: साधुः कारुणिको वाग्ग्मी वदेत्पुण्यां कथां सुधीः .. 23..
2.4.m: virtuous, compassionate, and eloquent, should recite the sacred story.
When the Purāṇa-reciter has mounted the seat of Vyāsa,
he should bow to no one until the end of the discourse.
A wise man should not recite the sacred story in a place crowded with wicked people,
nor in one overrun by śūdras or beasts of prey, nor in a gambling den.
Filled with faith and devotion, not longing for other business,
restrained in speech, pure, and attentive, the listeners share in merit.

2.4.s: abhaktā ye kathāṃ puṇyāṃ śṛṇvaṃti manujā'dhamāḥ ..
2.4.d: अभक्ता ये कथां पुण्यां शृण्वंति मनुजाऽधमाः ..
2.4.m: Those wretched men who listen to the sacred story without devotion—
they have no fruit of merit, and there is suffering for them birth after birth.
And at the end of the month, intent on devotion, one should honor the Purāṇa-reciter
with perfumes, garlands, as well as garments, ornaments, and wealth.

2.4.s: śṛṇvaṃti ca kathāṃ bhaktyā na daridrā na pāpinaḥ .. 29 ..
2.4.d: शृण्वंति च कथां भक्त्या न दरिद्रा न पापिनः .. 29 ..
2.4.m: Those who listen to the story with devotion are neither poor nor sinful.
Those men who go elsewhere while the story is being recited—
at the end of their enjoyment, their wives and riches perish.
A man seated on a high seat who does not bow down [in respect]
[becomes] a poisonous tree; and likewise, one who sleeps [during the recital] becomes a python in the forest.

2.4.s: kathāyāṃ kīrtyamānāyāṃ vighnaṃ kurvaṃti ye narāḥ ..
2.4.d: कथायां कीर्त्यमानायां विघ्नं कुर्वंति ये नराः ..
2.4.m: Those men who cause disruption while the story is being recited,
after suffering in hells for ten million years, become village pigs.

2.4.s: ye śrāvayaṃti manujāḥ kathāṃ paurāṇikīṃ śubhām ..
2.4.d: ये श्रावयंति मनुजाः कथां पौराणिकीं शुभाम् ..
2.4.m: Those men who cause the auspicious Purāṇic narrative to be heard
dwell in the realm of Brahmā for full hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Those men who provide for the Purāṇa-knower for the sake of a seat
blankets, antelope skins, cloths, a couch, or a wooden board,
and the men who provide garments to wear,
[and] provide ornaments and the like, shall dwell in the abode of Brahmā.

2.4.s: vācake parituṣṭe tu tuṣṭāḥ syuḥ sarvadevatāḥ ..
2.4.d: वाचके परितुष्टे तु तुष्टाः स्युः सर्वदेवताः ..
2.4.m: When the reciter is pleased, all the gods are pleased.
Therefore, a person endowed with devotion and faith should satisfy [him] with devotion.

2.4.s: tasya puṇyaphalaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ .. 36 ..
2.4.d: तस्य पुण्यफलं पूर्णं भवत्येव न संशयः .. 36 ..
2.4.m: His fruit of merit becomes complete indeed; there is no doubt.
Whatever fruit is obtained in all sacrifices and in all gifts,
a man attains that fruit just by hearing a Purāṇa once.
Especially in the Kali age, apart from the hearing of Purāṇas,

2.4.s: nāsti dharmaḥ paraḥ puṃsāṃ nāsti muktipathaḥ paraḥ ..
2.4.d: नास्ति धर्मः परः पुंसां नास्ति मुक्तिपथः परः ..
2.4.m: there is no higher dharma for men, no higher path to liberation.
Other than listening to Purāṇas and chanting the name of Viṣṇu, there is nothing higher.
Whoever hears this Ūrjamāhātmya or recites it to others,
he obtains the fruit of going to Badarī, king of sacred fords.
[It is] auspicious, removing all diseases and destroying all sins. (40)

2.4.s: śrutvā caikapade yo vai agamyāgamane rataḥ ..
2.4.d: श्रुत्वा चैकपदे यो वै अगम्यागमने रतः ..
2.4.m: And having heard it all at once, one who is devoted to approaching forbidden women,
and the seller of his daughter or sister—[this text] liberates both. (41)
Whoever, having heard this māhātmya, worships the reciter
with cows, land, gold, and garments—for he is indeed equal to Viṣṇu. (42)

2.4.s: dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇaṃ ca vedavidyādikaṃ ca yat ..
2.4.d: धर्मशास्त्रं पुराणं च वेदविद्यादिकं च यत् ..
2.4.m: The Dharmaśāstra, the Purāṇa, and whatever Vedic learning and the like [there is],
that book should indeed be given to the reciter by one desiring dharma.
For those who bestow the knowledge of the Purāṇas enjoy endless fruit. (43)

2.4.s: idaṃ yaḥ paṭhate bhaktyā śrutvā caivā'vadhārayet ..
2.4.d: इदं यः पठते भक्त्या श्रुत्वा चैवाऽवधारयेत् ..
2.4.m: Whoever reads this with devotion, and having heard it, holds it in mind,
is freed from all sins and goes to the realm of Viṣṇu. (44)
This must never be told to anyone devoid of faith, [or] evil-minded. (45)
Without worshipping the guru, the preacher of dharma, with foremost intellect and undivided mind,

2.4.s: bhuktvā tu bhogānnarakeṣu caiva tato hi janmāntara duḥkhabhogī .. 46 ..
2.4.d: भुक्त्वा तु भोगान्नरकेषु चैव ततो हि जन्मान्तर दुःखभोगी .. 46 ..
2.4.m: having experienced tortures in the hells, one will surely suffer misery in another birth. (46)
Therefore, one should worship with devotion the guru, the illuminator of truth. / This is only a fraction of the māhātmya that has been spoken by me to you, sinless one. (47)

2.4.s: māhātmyasya ca leśo'yaṃ tava cokto mayā'nagha .. 47 ..
2.4.d: माहात्म्यस्य च लेशोऽयं तव चोक्तो मयाऽनघ .. 47 ..
2.4.m: [This segment is included in the previous line / duplicate verse division: This is only a fraction of the māhātmya that has been spoken by me to you, sinless one. (47)]

2.4.s: na śakyate hi saṃpūrṇaṃ vaktuṃ varṣaśatairapi ..
2.4.d: न शक्यते हि संपूर्णं वक्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ..
2.4.m: For it cannot be spoken completely even in hundreds of years. / Formerly, on the summit of Kailāsa, Śiva spoke to Pārvatī; (48)
[Formerly, on the summit of Kailāsa, Śiva spoke to Pārvatī; (48)]
speaking the māhātmya of Kārtika for as long as a hundred years,
even so he did not reach the end; being unable [to complete it], he paused. (49)

2.4.s: putrārthī ca dhanārthī ca rājyārthī svaphalaṃ labhet ..
2.4.d: पुत्रार्थी च धनार्थी च राज्यार्थी स्वफलं लभेत् ..
2.4.m: One seeking a son, one seeking wealth, and one seeking a kingdom shall obtain their desired fruit.
What need of saying much here? One seeking liberation shall attain liberation. (50)
Sūta said:
Having been thus addressed by Brahmā, Nārada, overwhelmed with love,
bowed again and again and went away, a sage wandering at will. (51)
It was also told by Śaṃkara to his son out of a desire for his welfare;
hearing that speech of his father, the six-faced one was filled with joy. (52)
The majesty of Kārtika was also spoken by Kṛṣṇa to Satyabhāmā;
delighted by it, Satyā then performed the vow. (53)
The seers, having heard the supreme māhātmya from the Vālakhilyas,
became devoted to the vow of Ūrja; therefore, Ūrja is exceedingly dear. (54)
Having studied all the treatises, [this has been] extracted like the essence of milk;
there is no auspicious treatise equal to this, causing delight to Viṣṇu. (55)
Vyāsa said:
Having spoken thus to all those seers, Sūta, the foremost knower of dharma,

2.4.s: virarāma tataste tu pūjāṃ cakrustadāsya ca .. 56 ..
2.4.d: विरराम ततस्ते तु पूजां चक्रुस्तदास्य च .. 56 ..
2.4.m: then paused; and they then performed worship to him. (56)

2.4.s: te punaḥ svāśramaṃ gatvā hṛṣṭāste paramarṣayaḥ ..
2.4.d: ते पुनः स्वाश्रमं गत्वा हृष्टास्ते परमर्षयः ..
2.4.m: Having returned to their own hermitage, those supreme seers, being delighted,
performed the auspicious vow just as was taught by Sūta. (57)

2.4.s: anena vidhinā ye vai kurvaṃti kārtikavratam ..
2.4.d: अनेन विधिना ये वै कुर्वंति कार्तिकव्रतम् ..
2.4.m: Those who indeed perform the vow of Kārtika according to this rite,
they, freed from all sins, go to the dwelling of Viṣṇu. (58)

2.4.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe kārtikamāsamāhātmye puṣkariṇīsaṃjñikāṃtimatithitrayamāhātmyakathanapūrvakapurāṇa śravaṇamahimavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṭtriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 36 ..
2.4.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे कार्तिकमासमाहात्म्ये पुष्करिणीसंज्ञिकांतिमतिथित्रयमाहात्म्यकथनपूर्वकपुराण श्रवणमहिमवर्णनंनाम षट्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 36 ..
2.4.m: Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Listening to the Purāṇa Preceded by the Narration of the Māhātmya of the Final Three Lunar Days Named Puṣkariṇī,' in the Kārtikamāsamāhātmya in the second Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses]. (36)

2.4.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇe dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe saṭīkaṃ kārtikamāsamāhātmyaṃ samāptam ..
2.4.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराणे द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे सटीकं कार्तिकमासमाहात्म्यं समाप्तम् ..
2.4.m: Thus ends the Kārtikamāsamāhātmya with commentary, in the second Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Listening to the Purāṇa,' in the commentary on the Kārttikamāsamāhātmya composed by Harikṛṣṇa Śāstrī, son of Veṅkaṭarāma, crest-jewel of the astrologers' family. (36)
Now begins the fourth [section], the Kārtikamāsamāhātmya, in the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa (2.4):

2.4.m: 2. Brahmā speaks the duties of the Kārtika vow to Nārada; therein, on the topic of serving the guru, the history of Gautama's pupils Medhāvin, Kapila, and Sumati, and the vow duties; on the topic of gift of food, the story of the twice-born Satyaketu; on the topic of gift of cows, the history of the brahmin Sumati; on the topic of remembering the names [of God], narration of the history of Puṣkara; on the topic of the māhātmya of reciting the Gītā, narration of the history of Jaḍabrāhmaṇa; on the topic of the gift of stones, narration of the story of the brahmin woman. 137
