2.4.d: 7 विष्णुमंदिरे दीपदानमाहात्म्ये कुत्सद्विजकथानकम्, परदीपप्रबोधमाहात्म्यप्रसंगेनेन्दुमतीवेश्येतिहासकथनम्, आकाशदीपदानमाहात्म्यम्, खगमार्जारकथानकम, तत्रैव चन्द्रशर्मसुनन्दनृपसंवादेन कार्तिकव्रतधर्मनिरूपणम्, दीपमाहात्म्यम, आकाशदीपदानविधिः, आकाशदीपदानेन पिशाचमुक्तिकथनम्, पञ्चदिनेषु दीपदानम्, कार्तिकदीपकरणे स्थलानि, दीपदाने हरिकरब्राह्मणेतिहासः, कर्पूरदीपदानादिफलम्. 149
2.4.m: 7. In the māhātmya of offering lamps in a temple of Viṣṇu, the story of the twice-born Kutsa; on the topic of the māhātmya of kindling another's lamp, narration of the history of the courtesan Indumatī; māhātmya of the sky-lamp offering; the story of the bird and the cat; right there, determination of the duties of the Kārtika vow through the dialogue of Candraśarman and King Sunanda; māhātmya of lamps; rules for the sky-lamp offering; narration of the release of a piśāca through the sky-lamp offering; offering lamps on five days; places for making Kārtika lamps; the history of the brahmin Harikara concerning the offering of lamps; the fruit of offering camphor lamps and the like. 149
8. On the occasion of stating the māhātmya of tulasī, the history of the brahmins Harimedhas and Sumedhas. 153 1

2.4.s: 9 vatsadvādaśīvidhānam, pañcadīpe śakunāvalokanam, vatsadvādaśīvratenaikāṅgīgopālikāyā dhanadhānyasukhaprāptivṛttāntavarṇanam, yamatrayodaśīvidhānam, hemanakasyetihāsaḥ, narakacaturdaśīvidhānam, dīpāvalividhānam, tatra kaumudīśabdārthaḥ, pārvaṇaśrāddhādikaraṇam, sāyaṃ mahālakṣmīmahākālīmahāsarasvatīpūjā, lakṣmīprabodhotsavaprakaraṇam, dīpotsavanīrājanam, balirājyabālakrīḍāśubhāśubhaśakunāvalokanam, ardharātre'lakṣmyā bahirniṣkāsanam, sukharātrivratakathanam. .. 154 2
2.4.d: 9 वत्सद्वादशीविधानम्, पञ्चदीपे शकुनावलोकनम्, वत्सद्वादशीव्रतेनैकाङ्गीगोपालिकाया धनधान्यसुखप्राप्तिवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, यमत्रयोदशीविधानम्, हेमनकस्येतिहासः, नरकचतुर्दशीविधानम्, दीपावलिविधानम्, तत्र कौमुदीशब्दार्थः, पार्वणश्राद्धादिकरणम्, सायं महालक्ष्मीमहाकालीमहासरस्वतीपूजा, लक्ष्मीप्रबोधोत्सवप्रकरणम्, दीपोत्सवनीराजनम्, बलिराज्यबालक्रीडाशुभाशुभशकुनावलोकनम्, अर्धरात्रेऽलक्ष्म्या बहिर्निष्कासनम्, सुखरात्रिव्रतकथनम्. .. 154 2
2.4.m: 9. Rules for Vatsadvādaśī; observing omens through five lamps; description of the account of the single-limbed cowherdess obtaining wealth, grain, and happiness by the Vatsadvādaśī observance; rules for Yamatrayodaśī; the story of Hemanaka; rules for Narakacaturdaśī; rules for Dīpāvali; the meaning of the word kaumudī therein; performing the pārvaṇa-śrāddha and other rites; worship of Mahālakṣmī, Mahākālī, and Mahāsarasvatī in the evening; the chapter on the festival of awakening Lakṣmī; waving lamps (nīrājana) during the festival of lamps; children's games in Bali's kingdom and observing auspicious and inauspicious omens; driving Alakṣmī outside at midnight; narration of the Sukharātri observance. 154 2

2.4.s: 10 dyūtapratipadvarṇanam, balirājyapratipannirūpaṇam, pratipattithinirṇayaḥ, aṃgaṇe gomayamūrtipūjanam, govardhanapūjā, balīvardamahiṣavṛṣabhāṇāṃ yuddhakrīḍādarśanam, mārgapālīvidhiḥ, rātrau balipūjāvidhānam, gokrīḍāvarṇanam, yaṣṭiśakunāvalokanam. 158 2
2.4.d: 10 द्यूतप्रतिपद्वर्णनम्, बलिराज्यप्रतिपन्निरूपणम्, प्रतिपत्तिथिनिर्णयः, अंगणे गोमयमूर्तिपूजनम्, गोवर्धनपूजा, बलीवर्दमहिषवृषभाणां युद्धक्रीडादर्शनम्, मार्गपालीविधिः, रात्रौ बलिपूजाविधानम्, गोक्रीडावर्णनम्, यष्टिशकुनावलोकनम्. 158 2
2.4.m: 10. Description of the Gambling Pratipad; determination of Bali's Kingdom Pratipad; determining the Pratipad lunar day; worship of the cowdung image in the courtyard; worship of Govardhana; witnessing the playful fight of oxen, buffaloes, and bulls; the rite of the Mārgapālī; rules for worshipping Bali at night; description of the cow games; observing omens from the staff. 158 2
11. Rules for the Yamadvitīyā observance. 160

2.4.s: 12 dhātrīmāhātmyam, tatra dhātrīpūjāvidhiḥ, dhātrīvṛkṣotpattivṛttāntaḥ, dhātryāṃ devatānivāsavarṇanama, dhātrīcchāyāmāhātmyam, tatra vaiśyetihāsaḥ, kathāśravaṇena mūṣakamuktikathanam, dhātrīcchāyāyāṃ bhojanamāhātmyam, dhātrīcchāyāsu bhojanena doṣavināśavarṇanama, dhātrīmālādhāraṇam, dhātrīcchāyāyāṃ dīpamālārpaṇama, dhātrīcchāyāyāṃ daṃpatibhojanaphalam, dhātrīphalamāhātmyam, āmalakasnānaphalaṃ varjyakālaśca, dhātrīcchāyāyāṃ piṇḍadānaphalam, dhātrīphaladhāraṇe'ṅgāvayavaviśeṣavarṇanam, dhātrīcchāyāyāṃ brāhmaṇapūjanaphalam, dhātrīpūjāyāṃ tithayaḥ, vanabhojanavidhānam, dhātrīsparśamāhātmyam, gṛhe dhātrīvṛkṣamāhātmyam. 162
2.4.d: 12 धात्रीमाहात्म्यम्, तत्र धात्रीपूजाविधिः, धात्रीवृक्षोत्पत्तिवृत्तान्तः, धात्र्यां देवतानिवासवर्णनम, धात्रीच्छायामाहात्म्यम्, तत्र वैश्येतिहासः, कथाश्रवणेन मूषकमुक्तिकथनम्, धात्रीच्छायायां भोजनमाहात्म्यम्, धात्रीच्छायासु भोजनेन दोषविनाशवर्णनम, धात्रीमालाधारणम्, धात्रीच्छायायां दीपमालार्पणम, धात्रीच्छायायां दंपतिभोजनफलम्, धात्रीफलमाहात्म्यम्, आमलकस्नानफलं वर्ज्यकालश्च, धात्रीच्छायायां पिण्डदानफलम्, धात्रीफलधारणेऽङ्गावयवविशेषवर्णनम्, धात्रीच्छायायां ब्राह्मणपूजनफलम्, धात्रीपूजायां तिथयः, वनभोजनविधानम्, धात्रीस्पर्शमाहात्म्यम्, गृहे धात्रीवृक्षमाहात्म्यम्. 162
2.4.m: 12. The māhātmya of the Dhātrī tree; the procedure for worshipping the Dhātrī tree therein; the account of the origin of the Dhātrī tree; description of the dwelling of deities in the Dhātrī tree; the māhātmya of the Dhātrī tree's shade; the story of the vaiśya therein; the liberation of a mouse by listening to the story; the māhātmya of dining beneath the Dhātrī tree's shade; description of the destruction of sins by dining beneath the shades of Dhātrī trees; wearing a garland of Dhātrī berries; offering rows of lamps beneath the Dhātrī tree's shade; the fruit of a husband and wife dining beneath the Dhātrī tree's shade; the māhātmya of the Dhātrī fruit; the fruit of bathing with āmalaka and times when it is forbidden; the fruit of offering piṇḍas beneath the Dhātrī tree's shade; description of the specific limbs and body parts for wearing Dhātrī berries; the fruit of worshipping brahmins beneath the Dhātrī tree's shade; lunar days for worshipping the Dhātrī tree; rules for forest banquets (vanabhojana); the māhātmya of touching the Dhātrī tree; the māhātmya of a Dhātrī tree at home. 162

2.4.s: 13 satyabhāmākṛṣṇasaṃvāde satyabhāmāyāḥ pūrvajanmani kātikavratapuṇyena kṛṣṇabhāryātvaprāptirjāteti varṇanama, sarveṣāṃ madhye kārtikaḥ pravaraḥ kathamiti pṛṣṭena kṛṣṇena satyabhāmāṃ prati śaṃkhāsurākhyānena kārtikapravaratvanirūpaṇam, prayāgasthānamāhātmyama. 166 1
2.4.d: 13 सत्यभामाकृष्णसंवादे सत्यभामायाः पूर्वजन्मनि कातिकव्रतपुण्येन कृष्णभार्यात्वप्राप्तिर्जातेति वर्णनम, सर्वेषां मध्ये कार्तिकः प्रवरः कथमिति पृष्टेन कृष्णेन सत्यभामां प्रति शंखासुराख्यानेन कार्तिकप्रवरत्वनिरूपणम्, प्रयागस्थानमाहात्म्यम. 166 1
2.4.m: 13. In the dialogue between Satyabhāmā and Kṛṣṇa, the description of Satyabhāmā attaining the status of Kṛṣṇa's wife by the merit of the Kārtika observance in her previous birth; when asked how Kārtika is foremost among all [months], Kṛṣṇa's determination of Kārtika's supremacy addressed to Satyabhāmā by means of the story of the demon Śaṅkha; the māhātmya of the sacred site of Prayāga. 166 1

2.4.s: 14 tulasī kathamutpannā kathaṃ ca haripriyā jāteti pṛthunā pṛṣṭe nāradena tadutpattiṃ vaktumādāvindravajrapātena kruddhasya śivasya krodhāgninā jalandharotpattiprasaṃgavarṇanama... 167
2.4.d: 14 तुलसी कथमुत्पन्ना कथं च हरिप्रिया जातेति पृथुना पृष्टे नारदेन तदुत्पत्तिं वक्तुमादाविन्द्रवज्रपातेन क्रुद्धस्य शिवस्य क्रोधाग्निना जलन्धरोत्पत्तिप्रसंगवर्णनम... 167
2.4.m: 14. When asked by Pṛthu how Tulasī was born and how she became dear to Hari, Nārada, in order to tell of her origin, first describes the occasion of the birth of Jalandhara from the fire of anger of Śiva, who was enraged by Indra's thunderbolt strike. 167
15. Then, description of Jalandhara's victory in conquering the quarters; description of the reason for Bṛhaspati's obtaining the name Jīva. 168 1
16. Viṣṇu, praised by the gods who were defeated in battle, manifests and engages in combat. 169 1

2.4.s:
17 jalandharasabhāyāṃ nāradopadeśena strīratnasya pārvatyā grahaṇārthaṃ rāhupreṣaṇam, tena
kruddhasya śivasya bhrūmadhyātkīrtimukhagaṇotpattivarṇanam 169
2.4.d:
17 जलन्धरसभायां नारदोपदेशेन स्त्रीरत्नस्य पार्वत्या ग्रहणार्थं राहुप्रेषणम्, तेन
क्रुद्धस्य शिवस्य भ्रूमध्यात्कीर्तिमुखगणोत्पत्तिवर्णनम् 169
2.4.m: 17. The sending of Rāhu to seize Pārvatī, the jewel among women, upon Nārada's advice in Jalandhara's court; description of the birth of the gaṇa Kīrtimukha from the space between the eyebrows of Śiva, who was enraged thereby. 169
18. Then, in the war between the gods and the asuras, description of the defeat of Rudra's army. 170
19. The fall of Vīrabhadra. 171 2
20. Then, the great battle between Jalandhara and Śiva. 172 2

2.4.s: 21 vṛndāyāḥ pātivratyabhaṅgena jalaṃdharasya hananaṃ bhaviṣyatīti vicārya viṣṇunā vṛndāyai māyāpradarśanama, tato mithastayorviṣṇuvṛndayo śāpavṛttāntavarṇanam, vṛndayā dehavisarjane kṛte sati taddehabhasmani viṣṇorluṇṭhanam... ... 173 1
2.4.d: 21 वृन्दायाः पातिव्रत्यभङ्गेन जलंधरस्य हननं भविष्यतीति विचार्य विष्णुना वृन्दायै मायाप्रदर्शनम, ततो मिथस्तयोर्विष्णुवृन्दयो शापवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, वृन्दया देहविसर्जने कृते सति तद्देहभस्मनि विष्णोर्लुण्ठनम्... ... 173 1
2.4.m: 21. Considering that Jalandhara will be slain by the breach of Vṛndā's fidelity to her husband, Viṣṇu displays an illusion to Vṛndā; then, the account of the mutual curses between Viṣṇu and Vṛndā; upon Vṛndā's casting off her body, Viṣṇu's rolling in the ashes of her body. 173 1

2.4.s: 22 tato yuddhe jalaṃdharaṃ hatvā prasannatayā sthitasya śivasyā''jñayā viṣṇubodhanāya devairādiśaktīnāṃ stavanam , tatastuṣṭābhirdevībhirdevebhyo vistubodhanārthaṃ bījatrayapradānama., .... ... . 174 1
2.4.d: 22 ततो युद्धे जलंधरं हत्वा प्रसन्नतया स्थितस्य शिवस्या'ऽज्ञया विष्णुबोधनाय देवैरादिशक्तीनां स्तवनम् , ततस्तुष्टाभिर्देवीभिर्देवेभ्यो विस्तुबोधनार्थं बीजत्रयप्रदानम., .... ... . 174 1
2.4.m: 22. Then, having slain Jalandhara in battle, by the command of Śiva who was well pleased, the praise of the primal Śaktis by the gods to awaken Viṣṇu; then, the goddesses, being pleased, giving three seeds to the gods to awaken Viṣṇu. 174 1
23. From those seeds, the origin of Dhātrī, Mālatī, and Tulasī. 175 1
24. The release of Kalahā from her birth as a rākṣasī through the gift of the merit of Kārtika by Dharmadatta. 175 2

2.4.s: 25 kalahāvacanātkārtikamāse dānamāhātmyakathanam, viṣṇudūtānītavimānena samaṃ kalahāyā vaikuṇṭhaprāptiḥ, viṣṇudūtena tvaṃ janmāntare sūryavaṃśe daśarathetināmnā prasiddho rājā bhaviṣyasi tathaiva bhagavānviṣṇuḥ svayaṃ tvatputratvenāvatariṣyatīti dharmadattāya varapradānam 176 1
2.4.d: 25 कलहावचनात्कार्तिकमासे दानमाहात्म्यकथनम्, विष्णुदूतानीतविमानेन समं कलहाया वैकुण्ठप्राप्तिः, विष्णुदूतेन त्वं जन्मान्तरे सूर्यवंशे दशरथेतिनाम्ना प्रसिद्धो राजा भविष्यसि तथैव भगवान्विष्णुः स्वयं त्वत्पुत्रत्वेनावतरिष्यतीति धर्मदत्ताय वरप्रदानम् 176 1
2.4.m: 25. Because of Kalahā's words, the proclamation of the māhātmya of making gifts in the month of Kārtika; Kalahā's attainment of Vaikuṇṭha together with the aerial chariot brought by Viṣṇu's messengers; the granting of a boon to Dharmadatta by Viṣṇu's messenger: "In another birth you will become a renowned king named Daśaratha in the Solar dynasty, and likewise Lord Viṣṇu will incarnate himself as your son." 176 1
26. Narration of the māhātmya of devotion to Viṣṇu; on that occasion, description of the story of the Cola king and the twice-born Viṣṇudāsa. 177 1

2.4.s: 27 viṣṇudāsākhyadvijena svasya rūkṣānnāpaharaṇakāriṇaṃ caṃḍālaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasmai ghṛtapradānārthaṃ taṃ pratyanudhāvanam, tato mūrchitaṃ patitaṃ caṇḍālamavalokya tena viṣṇudāsena kṛpayā tasya caṇḍālasya satkārakaraṇam, tataścaṇḍālarūpadhāriṇā bhagavatā viṣṇudāsasyānugrahakaraṇam, bhagavatprasādādviṣṇudāsabrāhmaṇaṃ prati svargato vimānāgamanam, tasminnadhiruhya viṣṇudāse gacchati sati colarājenāgnipraveśanam, tato'smai bhagavatā svarūpadarśanam, colabhūpaviṣṇudāsabrāhmaṇayormuktiprāptiśca 177 2
2.4.d: 27 विष्णुदासाख्यद्विजेन स्वस्य रूक्षान्नापहरणकारिणं चंडालं दृष्ट्वा तस्मै घृतप्रदानार्थं तं प्रत्यनुधावनम्, ततो मूर्छितं पतितं चण्डालमवलोक्य तेन विष्णुदासेन कृपया तस्य चण्डालस्य सत्कारकरणम्, ततश्चण्डालरूपधारिणा भगवता विष्णुदासस्यानुग्रहकरणम्, भगवत्प्रसादाद्विष्णुदासब्राह्मणं प्रति स्वर्गतो विमानागमनम्, तस्मिन्नधिरुह्य विष्णुदासे गच्छति सति चोलराजेनाग्निप्रवेशनम्, ततोऽस्मै भगवता स्वरूपदर्शनम्, चोलभूपविष्णुदासब्राह्मणयोर्मुक्तिप्राप्तिश्च 177 2
2.4.m: 27. The twice-born named Viṣṇudāsa, seeing an outcaste stealing his dry food, running after him to give him clarified butter; then, seeing the outcaste fallen unconscious, Viṣṇudāsa showing hospitality to that outcaste out of compassion; then, the Lord, assuming the form of an outcaste, showing favor to Viṣṇudāsa; by the Lord's grace, the arrival of an aerial chariot from heaven for the brahmin Viṣṇudāsa; as Viṣṇudāsa mounts it and departs, the Cola king entering fire; then, the Lord revealing his true form to him; and both the Cola king and the brahmin Viṣṇudāsa attaining liberation. 177 2
28. Jaya and Vijaya attaining the status of Viṣṇu's doorkeepers by bathing in the Gaṇḍakī in Kārtika. 178 2
29. Description of Dhaneśvara attaining birth as a yakṣa through the merit of associating with those observing the Kārtika vow. 179 2
30. Description of the attainment of unbestowed merit and sin; the story of the devoted wife; the rules for the observance of fasting for a month. 180 1
31. The procedure for Kūṣmāṇḍanavamī; narration of the procedure for the marriage of Tulasī. 182 2
32. Rules for the Bhīṣmapañcaka observance. 183 21
33. The māhātmya of Prabodhinyekādaśī; rules for Dvādaśī. 185
34. Rules for concluding the Kārtika observance (udyāpana). 187 1
35. The māhātmya of Vaikuṇṭhacaturdaśī; the māhātmya of the Tripura festival. 188 1
36. The māhātmya of the lunar days of the final three sacred pools; description of the procedure and fruit of listening to the Purāṇa. 190 2
Now, in connection with the māhātmya of the month of Kārtika, the rules of what is to be done and what is not to be done by those observing vows in the month of Kārtika are stated. 1
Therein, the rules of what is to be done:

2.4.m: 1. Daily ritual ablution while the stars are visible. 2. Worship of Rādhā and Dāmodara. 3. Remembering the names of Viṣṇu, Hari, and Śiva. 4. Subduing the senses. 5. Restraint of the mind. 6. Compassion toward all beings. 7. Meditation on Īśvara. 8. Worship of Īśvara. 9. Speaking the truth. 10. Eating sacrificial food (haviṣyānna). 11. The vow of eating only at night (nakta). 12. The vow of alternate-day fasting (dhāraṇā-pāraṇā). 13. The vow of silence. 14. The vow of celibacy (brahmacarya). 15. Association with the good. 16. Worship of the emblic myrobalan (dhātrī) tree. 17. Worship of Viṣṇu in the shade of a dhātrī tree. 18. Daily listening to sacred stories. 19. Gift of land. 20. Service to mother and father. 21. Service to the guru. 22. Daily darśana of the deity. 23. Singing in the deity's temple. 24. Daily offering of lamps in the temple. 25. Offering lamps at crossroads. 26. Offering a lamp to a brahmin. 27. Offering a lamp in a cowshed. 28. Worship of tulasī. 29. Worship of the holy fig (aśvattha) tree. 30. Worship of deities, brahmins, and cows. 31. Circumambulation of the deity. 32. One hundred thousand circumambulations of tulasī. 33. Circumambulation of an aśvattha tree. 34. Feeding brahmins. 35. Gift of food. 36. Gift of a cow, a bull, a buffalo-cow, and an elephant. 37. Gift of gold, metals, and jewels. 38. Protection of the helpless. One should strictly practice these observances in the month of Kārtika.

2.4.m: 1. Desiring another's property. 2. Acting on another's behalf [without right]. 3. Slandering others. 4. [Sleeping in] another's bed. 5. Another's food. 6. Stale food. 7. Onions. 8. Association with sinners. 9. Intercourse with another man. 10. Approaching another's wife. 11. Malice toward others. 12. Intolerance of another's superiority. 13. Proclaiming another's faults. 14. Thinking of harm to others. 15. Untrue chatter. 16. Approaching a forbidden woman. 17. Inedible food. 18. What is forbidden by the scriptures. 19. Meat dishes. 20. Bad scriptures. 21. Lack of faith in scripture. 22. Theft. 23. Falsehood. 24. Association with the wicked. 25. Wicked speech. 26. Meat. 27. Milk from a cow whose calf has died. 28. Food seen by a menstruating woman. 29. Water brought by an outcaste. 30. Cow-milk mixed with jaggery. 31. Kidney beans (rājamāṣa). 32. Eating and drinking from a bronze vessel. 33. Pulses. 34. Eggplant. 35. Radish. 36. [Application of] oil. 37. Contaminated food. 38. Citron (jambīra). 39. Sexual indulgence by day. 40. Daily sexual indulgence. 41. Selling liquids/sap. One must strictly avoid these in the month of Kārtika.
Thus ends the determination of what is to be done and what is to be avoided in the month of Kārtika.

2.4.m:
On the bright ninth of Mārgaśīrṣa, Sampāti announced to the monkeys that she was dwelling in Rāvaṇa's abode in the tenth month. 27 / On the eleventh, Hanūmān leaped a hundred yojanas from Mount Mahendra; / on that very night he searched through Laṅkā. / At the end of that night, Hanūmān indeed had the darśana of Sītā. 29 / On the twelfth, Hanūmān stationed himself in the śiṃśapā tree; / on that night there was conversation with Jānakī to gain her trust. 30 / On the thirteenth, battle then took place with Akṣa and the others. / On the fourteenth, the monkey was bound by Indrajit with the Brahmā weapon; 31 / the burning of Laṅkā was done with his fire-lit tail. / On the full moon day occurred the monkey's return to Mount Mahendra. - Padmapurāṇa 5.36.32
The great Kārttikī at Puṣkara, and at Kānyakubja likewise further... 128 ... the great [full moon] in Mārgaśīrṣa would be... - Bhaviṣyapurāṇa 2.2.8.128
Nārada 1.18 (The observance and concluding rite for the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa),
"On the full moon of Mārgaśīrṣa, an āḍhaka measure of salt accompanied by gold / should be given to a tranquil brahmin for the fulfillment of all desires." — Nārada Purāṇa 1.124.67.

"Milk in the month of Āśvayuja, ghee mixed with curd in Kārtika, / cow-urine in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, and clarified butter in Pauṣa should be consumed." — Matsya Purāṇa 60.35.
"Then was born the son named Pūṣan on an auspicious day in Mārgaśīrṣa; / he, devoted to the science of astronomy, worshiped the sun. (115)
By the grace of the God of gods, he attained liberation in the sun. / Therefore, O king of the gods, worship the sun in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa!" — Bhaviṣya Purāṇa 3.4.8.116.
